records.title: Director of Quality and Survey
records.description:
At Vetter Senior Living, our mission is simple: **Dignity in Life**. We are a premier provider of long-term care, assisted living, independent living, therapy, and home health and hospice services, and our team of skilled and caring people is committed to making quality service a way of life. Our work is guided by our values of Serving, Integrity, Teamwork, and Excellence.

**About the Role**

We are seeking a Director of Quality and Survey to provide quality and survey leadership and support to our communities. Through strong personal relationships, you will help our communities and service lines ensure that quality and regulatory requirements are not only met but exceeded. This role travels between communities and serves as a trusted clinical and regulatory resource for facility leadership.

### **Benefits**

* Student Loan Repayment Assistance
* Earned Wage Access
* Medical Insurance Options
* Vision Coverage
* Free Individual Dental Insurance
* 401(k) with Employer Match
* Flexible Spending Accounts
* Employee Assistance Program
* Leadership Development Opportunities
* Career Growth and Advancement
* Supportive Senior Leadership Team
* Great Place to Work® Certified Organization

**What You Will Do**

* Monitor compliance with federal and state regulations and maintain ongoing survey readiness in skilled nursing and assisted living.
* Identify potential deficiencies early and help facility leadership develop corrective actions.
* Conduct focused and routine audits of high-risk areas such as falls, wounds, infections, medication management, hospital transfers, documentation, and changes in condition.
* Manage the iQIES and HARP systems for the organization.
* Support facility Quality Assurance and Performance Improvement (QAPI) activities by identifying trends, establishing improvement plans, monitoring results, and evaluating whether interventions are working.
* Provide targeted education and coaching to Directors of Nursing, nurse leaders, and clinical teams when audits or quality data reveal knowledge or process gaps.
* Drive corrective actions such as staff education, coaching, focused chart reviews, and process changes.
* Serve as a clinical and regulatory resource to facility leadership on complex compliance, resident-care, documentation, or risk concerns.
* Partner with leadership while maintaining facility accountability for day-to-day operations.
* Promote continuous improvement in quality and survey processes and outcomes, and support all Vetter Senior Living service lines and growth opportunities.

**What You Bring**

* Licensed nurse (RN preferred).
Minimum of 3* -5 years of experience in post-acute care.
* Experience managing quality outcomes, with a strong understanding of regulations and survey preparation and management.
* Excellent communication and education skills.
* Strong organizational and relationship-building skills.
* Ability and willingness to travel between communities.
* High personal integrity, a caring attitude, and a genuine desire to work with and support others.

**Why Join Us**

You will be part of a highly respected team of skilled and caring people who are committed to making quality service a way of life. Your daily efforts will help our communities deliver exceptional care, and you will find fulfillment in building relationships, coordinating care, and helping enhance the dignity in people's lives.

**Ready to make a difference? Apply today to join the Vetter Senior Living team.**

records.title: Senior Manager Operational Area Quality (Hybrid)
records.description:
**Job Description**

**General/Position Summary**

 

The Quality Assurance Senior Operational Manager is recognized as an expert internally in the principles and application of quality assurance and compliance. The Quality Snr Manager will provide QA support of manufacturing operations, analytical laboratory operations and materials management for the external manufacture of Cell & Genetic Therapeutic programs. This role will drive, review & support activities related to product disposition including review of batch data, batch records, deviations, in-process data, EM data, QC release testing and other quality systems documentation.

 

**Key Duties & Responsibilities**

* Responsible for quality support of Vertex Cell and Gene Therapy manufacturing operations across all phases of development, support of analytical laboratory, materials management and manufacturing operations.

* Responsible for GMP batch disposition activities including review and approval of batch records, deviations, in-process data, EM data, QC release testing, materials review board and other quality activities as applicable to determine acceptability of product disposition.

* Partner with External CDMOs

* Provide QA support of change controls, process and OOS investigations, and associated CAPAs.

* Responsible for approval of COAs and product labelling.

* Support review and approval of manufacturing documents such as technical and analytical protocols/reports

* Support technical transfer, and process performance qualification activities.

* Responsible for identifying compliance risks and gaps for GMP processes and supporting implementation of mitigating controls

* Support audit and inspection readiness activities.

* Act as a trusted advisor by providing compliance guidance through collaborative review and partnering with business stakeholders and contract manufacturers.

* Support the vendor management process including the creation and review of Quality Agreements with suppliers.

* Assist with addressing product complaints

* Maintain periodic batch record metrics and assists department with routine/quarterly Quality System data review metrics and reporting

* Execute improvements to QA operations procedure.

* Participate/ lead Cell & Genetic Program and Quality projects and drive continuous improvement activities.

 

**Required Education Level**

* Bachelor's degree in a biotech/ Lifesciences field.

* Preferred Master's degree or relevant comparable background.

 

**Required Experience**

8+ years of relevant industry experience such as manufacturing, quality assurance, and/or quality control in biotechnology/regulated pharmaceutical environment.

 

**Required Knowledge/Skills**

* Demonstrated experience providing QA support to GMP manufacturing operation
* Experience successfully leading event investigations, Root Cause Analysis and CAPA
* Experience with network-based applications such as Oracle, TrackWise, Veeva
* In-depth knowledge of both the conceptual and practical application of cGMPs in a pharmaceutical setting; Biotech/Cell & Gene GMP regulations and applicability. (e.g. EU, FDA, ICH, USP, etc. or other industry best practices ex. ISPE, WHO, etc.)
* Knowledge in Cell technology, aseptic manufacturing technology, analytical assays, cell & genetic therapies/Biologics processing, fill/finish and testing.
* Professional membership or equivalent in relevant societies, network of knowledge in cell and gene therapy industry.
* Ability to evaluate quality matters and make decisions utilizing risk-based approach
Ability to independently lead cross-functional teams, and effectively communicate with business stakeholders. 

 

**Other Requirements**

Up to 15% Travel may be required 

 
 

At Vertex, we embrace continuous learning and encourage employees to stay informed on advances in AI, technology, automation, and industry trends. We seek talent who bring an external perspective, demonstrate curiosity and sound judgment, and thoughtfully adopt new capabilities that improve decision-making, drive innovation, increase efficiency, and help deliver better outcomes for patients.

**Pay Range:**

$133,800 - $200,600

**Disclosure Statement:**

The range provided is based on what we believe is a reasonable estimate for the base salary pay range for this job at the time of posting. This role is eligible for an annual bonus and annual equity awards. Some roles may also be eligible for overtime pay, in accordance with federal and state requirements. Actual base salary pay will be based on a number of factors, including skills, competencies, experience, and other job-related factors permitted by law.

At Vertex, our Total Rewards offerings also include inclusive market-leading benefits to meet our employees wherever they are in their career, financial, family and wellbeing journey while providing flexibility and resources to support their growth and aspirations. From medical, dental and vision benefits to generous paid time off (including a week-long company shutdown in the Summer and the Winter), educational assistance programs including student loan repayment, a generous commuting subsidy, matching charitable donations, 401(k) and so much more.

**Flex Designation:**

Hybrid-Eligible Or On-Site Eligible

**Flex Eligibility Status:**

In this Hybrid-Eligible role, you can choose to be designated as:
 
1. **Hybrid** : work remotely up to two days per week; **or select** 
2. **On-Site** : work five days per week on-site with ad hoc flexibility.

Note: The Flex status for this position is subject to Vertex’s Policy on Flex @ Vertex Program and may be changed at any time.

#LI-Hybrid

**Company Information**

Vertex is a global biotechnology company that invests in scientific innovation.

Vertex is committed to equal employment opportunity and non-discrimination for all employees and qualified applicants without regard to a person's race, color, sex, gender identity or expression, age, religion, national origin, ancestry, ethnicity, disability, veteran status, genetic information, sexual orientation, marital status, or any characteristic protected under applicable law. Vertex is an E-Verify Employer in the United States. Vertex will make reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with known disabilities, in accordance with applicable law.

Any applicant requiring an accommodation in connection with the hiring process and/or to perform the essential functions of the position for which the applicant has applied should make a request to the recruiter or hiring manager, or contact Talent Acquisition at ApplicationAssistance@vrtx.com

records.title: Senior Manager, Manufacturing Quality
records.description:
At GE Appliances, a Haier company, we come together to make “good things, for life.” As the fastest-growing appliance company in the U.S., we’re powered by creators, thinkers and makers who believe that anything is possible and that there’s always a better way. We believe in the power of our people and in giving them the freedom to explore, discover and build good things, together.

 

The GE Appliances philosophy, backed by three simple commitments defines the way we work, invent, create, do business, and serve our communities: *we come together*, *we always look for a better way*, and *we create possibilities*.

Candidates must be legally authorized to work in the United States at the time of hire and must be able to maintain such authorization without current or future employer or school sponsorship. GE Appliances will not sponsor employment-based visas for this position now or in the future.

Interested in joining us on our journey?

 
The Senior Manager, Manufacturing Quality leads a team supporting the execution of short-term and long term projects focused on product and process quality improvement. The role supports front-line leadership and development of both salary and hourly team members in support of the factory Manufacturing Control Plans. The role is responsible for working cross-functionally to execute the overall goal for reducing the cost of poor quality associated with plant operations and product performance post-sale.

**Position**
------------

Senior Manager, Manufacturing Quality

**Location**
------------

USA, Louisville, KY

**How You'll Create Possibilities**
-----------------------------------

* Live, promote and support the Appliance Production System (APS) philosophy and drive continuous improvement in the quality and adjacent areas. Coach all team members to ensure cross-functional, focused collaboration is the way we work.
* Partner with the Quality Improvement Engineering, Business Operations and Manufacturing Engineering Leaders to promote a culture that establishes, sustains and improves product quality through engineering problem solving and discipline around supporting systems. Promote a method-based quick response to new issues.
* Responsible for developing and tracking team performance metrics tied to the overall factory (FPY, EOLA, Scrap) and effect to the product line financial plan (Damage, Scrap). Leads the team to complete projects and tasks supporting this effort. Owns and assigns tasks and establishes accountability at the appropriate level.
* Closely collaborates with the product line Engineering, Field Quality and Service organizations to understand and respond to part or system product level performance issues impacting owner use and satisfaction. Responds to this data in addition to internal data streams (leading indicators) for product quality and reliability (Engineering, EOLA and audit labs).
* Identify and execute projects to improve the cost of operations. Serve as a broad owner for Corrective and Preventative Actions (CAPA), Corrective Action Request (CAR) approach to problem solving.
* Owner of the execution of attributes of the Manufacturing Control Plan for broad areas. Responsible for the training, execution, auditing and improvement of the Manufacturing Quality Control Plan. Support efforts intended to improve workstation documentation process; create, update and maintain Manufacturing Control Instructions (MCI’s), visual aid and alerts (single point lessons) as needed.
* Strong technical aptitude and ability to coach others in complex engineering topics like dimensional control, material properties, failure analysis as well as emerging technologies such as AI
* Support analysis of data as part of Statistical Process Control (SPC) and implementation of responses as required by MCI/MCP. Escalate and measure response to data trends. Validate root cause response for effectiveness.
* Lead and support 1x1 problem solving for quality systems and related issues collaborate cross functionally to improve product quality through the identification and elimination of root cause of issues. Focus on overall repair efficiency.

**What You'll Bring to Our Team**
---------------------------------

* 8+ Years of successful experience in Manufacturing / Quality, focused on providing operational support to support operations and vertical manufacturing operations.
* Demonstrated expertise in a combination of Metrology, CMM or 3D scanning of complicated assemblies
* Ability to work within large cross-functional teams and at multiple levels in the organization.
* Demonstrated excellent communication, presentation, and facilitation skills.
* Demonstrated experience as a hands-on problem solver including complex systems (supply, build, testing and diagnosis)
* Demonstrated leadership during technically challenging and complicated cross functional projects/tasks

**Desired Characteristics**

* Engineering degree with strong content tied to understanding and impact to business financial performance
* Quality Leadership experience
* Prior experience in a union environment
* Strong organizational skills- focused on project and resource management

### **Working Conditions**

### 

* Working conditions are normal for a high-volume manufacturing environment.
* Working in this environment will occasionally require the use of safety equipment to include but not limited to: eye safety glasses, hearing protectors, work boots, and hardhats.
* These roles require frequent walking in a manufacturing plant environment.
* Travel (up to 10%) to suppliers and other manufacturing locations as needed.
* This position will be located in Louisville, KY.
* Hours & Weekends: Working off-shift and weekends may be required.

**Our Culture**
---------------

Our work is centered on our People and Culture as reflected in our Zero Distance philosophy and we recognize the importance of reaffirming our commitment to inclusion and diversity (I&D). This underscores our commitment to fostering an environment where every individual feels valued, connected, and empowered to contribute, while positioning our organization to adapt seamlessly to the evolving needs of our workforce and communities. 
 
This reflects our dedication to creating solutions that: Empower colleagues by fostering an environment where all voices are heard, valued, and encouraged to contribute. Strengthen communities where we live and work. Reinforce a culture of belonging, purpose, and engagement. Reflect the diversity of the communities we serve through our workforce, products, and practices. 
 
By further embedding Zero Distance into our People and Culture framework, we will continue to build a deeply connected organization. We are cultivating a culture of engagement, belonging, and connection, because while attracting new talent remains a priority, retention is a cornerstone of our strategy.

GE Appliances is a trust-based organization. It is important we offer our employees the flexibility they need to do their best work while balancing the needs of the business and individuals. When you join GE Appliances, you will have the opportunity to work with your leader to create a flexible work arrangement that balances the needs of the individual, team, and organization.

GE Appliances is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, national or ethnic origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, disability, protected veteran status or other characteristics protected by law.

GE Appliances participates in E-Verify and will provide the federal government with your Form I-9 information to confirm that you are authorized to work in the U.S

*If you are an individual with a disability and need assistance or an accommodation to use our website or to apply, please send an e-mail* *to ask.recruiting@geappliances.com*

records.title: Plant Manager
records.description:
We are seeking a skilled Plant Manager to oversee our co-manufacturing operations. The Plant Manager will be responsible for managing all aspects of plant operations while ensuring efficient production processes and maintaining high standards of quality and safety. This role requires strong leadership abilities, strategic thinking, and a deep understanding of manufacturing operations in a co-manufacturing setting.
 
 
**Responsibilities:** 

* Operational Leadership: Lead day-to-day plant operations, including production, packaging, maintenance, and quality control, to achieve production targets and quality standards.
* Team Management: Supervise and mentor a team of managers, supervisors, technicians, and support staff, fostering a culture of safety, quality, teamwork, accountability, and continuous improvement.
* Production Planning: Develop and implement production schedules and resource allocation plans to optimize efficiency and meet customer demand while minimizing costs.
* Quality Assurance: Ensure adherence to quality assurance protocols and regulatory requirements, implementing corrective actions as needed to address non-conformities and improve processes.
* Safety and Compliance: Maintain a safe working environment by enforcing safety policies and procedures, conducting regular safety audits, and promoting a culture of safety awareness among employees.
* Budget and Cost Control: Manage plant budget and expenses effectively, identifying opportunities for cost savings and implementing measures to improve operational efficiency.
* Supplier and Customer Relations: Collaborate with suppliers and co-manufacturing partners to ensure timely delivery of materials and finished goods, and build strong relationships with customers to understand their needs and preferences.
* Continuous Improvement: Drive continuous improvement initiatives, such as Lean Manufacturing or Six Sigma methodologies, to streamline processes, reduce waste, and enhance overall plant performance.
* Reporting and Analysis: Prepare regular reports on plant performance, including production metrics, quality metrics, and financial KPIs, and provide analysis and recommendations for improvement to senior management.

**Qualifications:** 

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Operations Management, Business Administration, or a related field; Master’s degree preferred.
* Proven experience (10+ years) in a managerial role within a co-manufacturing or food production environment.
* Strong understanding of manufacturing processes, quality standards, and regulatory requirements.
* Excellent leadership and interpersonal skills, with the ability to motivate and develop a diverse team.
* Strategic thinker with a track record of driving operational excellence and achieving business objectives.
* Proficiency in ERP systems and Microsoft Office Suite; experience with manufacturing software (e.g., SAP, Oracle) is a plus.
* Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities, with a focus on data-driven decision-making.
* Certification in Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, or other relevant certifications is desirable.
* #LI-JO1

Maker's Pride is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

records.title: Director, Program Operations
records.description:
In this role, the Director of Program Operations leads a team of Operations Program Managers (OPM) and Material Program Managers (MPM) responsible for the operational elements of program execution within Mercury's IPS business unit. This role serves as the primary conduit between the line of business and operational teams, ensuring seamless coordination across engineering, supply chain, manufacturing, and growth functions.

You will be responsible for developing and executing operational program plans for critical programs, overall ownership of operational program performance, and internal communication of customer requirements affecting operational execution.

The Director of Program Operations will support proposals by providing accurate basis of cost estimates, focusing on supply chain material costs in addition to manufacturing labor costs. This work will be performed in conjunction with factory operations, supply chain, and engineering functions. Candidates must have excellent written and oral communications skills to influence across multiple functions and communicate effectively with external partners.

This role is on site at one of the following Mercury facilities: **Torrance, CA**

**Job Responsibilities:**

* Lead, coach, and develop a team of OPMs and MPMs accountable for operational aspects of program life cycle from proposal, development, production, sustainment, & delivery.
* Serve as the primary liaison between the line of business and operations, communicating customer requirements that affect manufacturing and supply chain execution.
* Responsible for meeting the financial objectives of the business unit, including the management of Estimate at Completion (EACs) specific to operations labor and material content.
* Oversee supply chain and manufacturing milestones to ensure compliance with contract baseline.
* Monitor program risks and opportunities, including obsolescence management, reporting, and improvement actions.
* Support and present operations metrics and data through program reviews (both internal and external) to Mercury and customer leadership.
* Champion efforts to meet readiness requirements throughout an NPI stage-gate process.
* Change leader, helping to drive Mercury's strategy, structure, and values.
* Strategic thinking coupled with ROI / business case development.

**Required Qualifications:**

* Bachelor's degree
* Typically requires 10+ years prior relevant experience in functional areas of Supply Chain, Operations (including Production Control), Program Management, or technical Project Management.
* Strong financial acumen with experience providing input into and reviewing EACs, along with development of business cases.
* Experience in review and understanding of Statements of Work (SOW) and project requirements (technical and commercial).
* Strong analytical skills, problem‑solving capabilities, and attention to detail.
* Experience developing and mentoring high‑performing teams.
* Excellent communication skills (written, verbal, and presentation), leadership abilities, and the ability to work in an IPT environment.
* The ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. government issued security clearance is required. U.S. citizenship is required, as only U.S. citizens are eligible for a security clearance.

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* A self-starter, capable of achieving organizational and program objectives, and able to interface with all levels of internal management and external stakeholders.
* Ability to succeed in fast paced, developmental environment.
* Excellent time management skills and the ability to assign the appropriate priorities to the many tasks that need to be performed.
* Knowledge of US Government acquisition laws and regulations (FAR).
* Proficiency in ERP/MRP business systems.
* Knowledge of Mercury-type products.

#LI-RL1

**Why should you join Mercury Systems?**

Mercury Systems is a technology company that makes the world a safer, more secure place. We push processing power to the tactical edge, making the latest commercial technologies profoundly more accessible for today's most challenging aerospace and defense missions. From silicon to system scale, Mercury enables customers to accelerate innovation and turn data into decision superiority. Headquartered in Andover, Massachusetts, Mercury employs more than 2,300 people in 24 locations worldwide. To learn more, visit mrcy.com

**Our Culture**

We are committed to making Mercury a great place to work, no matter where our employees are located. We offer a casual and enjoyable atmosphere that allows employees to learn and grow. We help and care for one another and work as one to achieve results for us and for our customers. We value communication and transparency, and strive to foster two-way dialogue at all levels of the organization. We are committed to lifelong learning, offering comprehensive skills training and tuition reimbursement. Whether you're just starting out on your career journey or you are an experienced professional, it's important to us that you feel recognized and rewarded for your contributions.

To find out more about Why Mercury?, or visit the Mercury Community or find answers to general questions at Mercury FAQs

Mercury Systems is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex (including pregnancy), sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, genetic information, creed, citizenship, disability, protected veteran or marital status.

As an equal opportunity employer, Mercury Systems is committed to a diverse workforce. In addition to base salary, Mercury provides a variety of benefits for team members including:

records.title: Sr. Manager, Quality
records.description:
At Bloom Energy, our vision for a world powered by clean, reliable, and affordable energy is more than just a dream—we’re making it reality.

 

For over two decades, we’ve been at the forefront of the global energy transition, pioneering solutions that empower critical industries to thrive in a rapidly digitizing, energy-intensive world. From revolutionizing power for AI-driven data centers to ensuring resilience for hospitals, electric grids, manufacturing facilities, and utilities, our solid oxide fuel cell (SOFC) and solid oxide electrolyzer (SOEC) technologies are redefining what’s possible by delivering energy abundance for all. With more than 30,000 fuel cell modules deployed worldwide, we are the trusted partner for Fortune 100 companies and innovators alike. Our cutting-edge solutions enable unparalleled “time-to-power” capabilities, reliability, and sustainability, ensuring our customers remain ahead in a world where soaring energy demand and intensifying energy scarcity are rapidly becoming the new norm.

At Bloom, we thrive on collaboration, bold thinking, and relentless innovation. We believe that, together, we can create a brighter, more sustainable future while tackling the most pressing challenges of the 21st century.

 

We are looking for a S **r. Manager, Quality** to join our team in one of today’s most exciting technologies. This role will report to **Director of Quality** and based in **Newark, Delaware. This is a fully on-site, in office role 5 days a week** .

 

**Role and Responsibilities:**

* Ensure 100% Quality assurance at the Skid line manufacturing through inspection, testing, and sub-component testing/inspection. Assist in hiring personnel needed to support this effort.

* Partner with Install Quality team (field) to understand real time (daily) what items are escaping the plant and instituting immediate mitigation plans including addressing any inventory in the pipeline not yet installed.

* Implement permanent corrective actions working with Manufacturing, Engineering, Supply chain, or SQE as per relevance on each issue.

* Provide quality input into the new equipment being purchased for the scaling of Delaware manufacturing. Include inputs for quality assurance into equipment design, and verification of process steps. Understand and provide input into the planned operation, what can be bypassed, maintenance plans, calibration or drift of the equipment, automation that can fail and be undetected leading to quality escapes.

* Participate and understand results from testing in the plant; Functional test, Tommy test, FIT, etc. Drive pareto of failures to help cross functional problem solving of test failures.

* Implement a 100% functional test (new) on skid final product assembly; electrical continuity, communications integrity, piping assurance, start up simulation, etc. to assure 100% QA prior to shipping to customer.

* Ensure skid components and systems have latest FW revision prior to shipping to the W/H, or out of W/H to field.

* Work with CIG and Manufacturing Engr, and NPI to implement workload being removed from the customer install side and being moved into skid assembly. Provide oversight to ensure best quality achievement; ensure work instructions are clear, operators trained, workstations have proper tools, and judgement criteria.

* Collaborate with Supplier Quality / Suppliers to achieve zero-defect flow (“dock-to-stock”) for all purchased, contract manufacture parts, materials, and Bloom Energy manufactured parts.

* Drive component and design failures back to the earliest point of detection in the process.

* Ensure manufacturing process have Control plans with CTQ, and POA built in to each station.

* Work collaboratively with Design teams to DFM, through a “registration system”, and Pokeyoke assembly methods for highest quality assurance.

* Drive test excellence in the manufacturing plan to ensure that equipment and test stations are certified with robust qualification programs, that are documented and controlled for changes with proper accuracy and gage R&R techniques.

* Drive yield task forces to achieve company wide targets at each manufacturing point under this scope, with cross functional teams driving top pareto issues to RCCA.

* Ensure early engagement with the product engineering team to teach and perform early stage risk assessments (DFMEA et.al.)

* Design for manufacturability and reliability improvements during the early design stages of product development.

* Work with Engineering NPI and the manufacturing engineering teams to perform PFMEA, write work instructions, and establish quality check-points to guarantee zero-defect quality in production.

* Develop and implement formal, comprehensive process documentation including process flow diagrams, Process FMEAs, process control plans, operations method Sheets, manufacturing quality charts (MQCs) and etc.

* Lead critical problem solving task forces with emphasis on cross functional inputs, accountability, time to RCCA, and ensurance of mitigation of inventory, or field units at risk.

* Troubleshoot product issues by reviewing engineering drawings and design requirements. Drive a rigorous resolution process for product quality, reliability and design issues.

* Perform data-driven root cause failure analyses for design, manufacturing, and administrative problems.

* Perform process audits to monitor, continuously improve, and sustain superior product quality.

* Demonstrate the ability to interface and work collaboratively across departments internally and with suppliers and customers, (including Purchasing, Quality, R&D, Manufacturing, Product Engineering, Marketing and Finance), while building strong and cooperative working relationships.

* Cost of Poor Quality (COPQ) Reduction: Establish and govern site COPQ metrics (scrap, rework, sorting, and warranty risk); lead cross-functional yield-improvement blitzes targeting measurable cost reductions and scrap minimization.

* Process Capability & Zero-Defect Mentality: Drive process capability (C\_p / C\_{pk} \ge 1.33) across critical-to-quality (CTQ) operations (welding, brazing, ceramic stack assembly, plumbing/gas-delivery, and electrical integration).

 

**Skills and Experience:**

* More than 10 years of increasing responsibility in the areas of Quality, and Manufacturing .

* Experience implementing company-wide ISO 9001 procedures and TS16949 standards and related process documentation. Possess working knowledge of process capability and control requirements, methods and systems.

* Demonstrated track record of building, restructuring, or significantly scaling a manufacturing quality team during rapid production ramp-up

* Proven successful application of multi-discipline engineering problem solving techniques.

* Understand the critical elements of modern Manufacturing Statistical Process Control, (e.g., practical working knowledge and experience with SPC, Process Capability, Cp, Cpk, etc.)

* Understand the critical elements of modern Reliability Engineering, (e.g., MCF, MTBF, MTT, etc.)

* Certification in a recognized problem-solving methodology such as six-sigma Black Belt, 8D, or Global Problem Solving.

* Strong verbal/active listening/written communications.

* Demonstrate planning and leadership skills.

* Expert with metrology, calibration, and Gage R & R’s.

* Ability to train in Quality System Auditing.

* Direct experience managing high-temperature fluidics/gas delivery, welding/brazing, ceramic integration, power electronics, or structural enclosures is a strong plus.

records.title: Director of Practice and ASC Operations
records.description:
**Director of Practice and ASC Operations**

Reporting to: Chief Operating Officer

**About the Role**

Lead the day-to-day business operations of a multi-provider pain management practice and ambulatory surgery center (ASC). Your initial priorities will be to make it easier for patients and referring offices to reach us, convert more referrals into scheduled visits, and make better use of clinic and procedure capacity.

**A core part of the role is using data, technology, and automation to improve how the practice and ASC operate as they grow.** You’ll use call, referral, and scheduling data to see where patients get stuck and where capacity goes unused. You’ll then redesign workflows, improve how teams use existing systems, and automate repetitive steps such as routing callbacks or flagging referrals that need follow-up. You’ll measure whether those changes improve access, reduce manual work, and free up staff time.

This is a hands-on leadership role. You’ll lead staff, set clear expectations, and work directly with physicians and the ASC Director of Nursing to improve how the practice and surgery center operate. We welcome leaders from healthcare and other complex service businesses. You’ll bring experience leading a team, using data to identify problems, and carrying changes through to measurable results.

**What You Bring**

**Required**

* Progressive operations leadership experience with direct responsibility for hiring, coaching, developing, and managing the performance of a team.
* Experience running a complex, customer-facing operation and managing the drivers of financial performance, such as labor, capacity, productivity, and operating expenses.
* A track record of personally leading workflow improvements that produced measurable, sustained results in access, service, efficiency, or cost.
* Experience using data and KPIs to identify bottlenecks, prioritize action, and verify that changes improved performance.
* Experience using technology or automation to simplify workflows, reduce manual work, and help staff adopt new ways of working.
* Ability to lead changes that span teams, take ownership when progress stalls, and work hands-on with frontline staff to resolve problems.
* Bachelor’s degree or equivalent relevant experience.

**What success looks like**

* **Better patient access.** Make it easier for patients to connect with us and stay engaged throughout their care. Answer more calls live, return messages promptly, and offer convenient online scheduling for eligible visits. Use technology alongside personal outreach to keep patients informed, respond to their needs, and support them throughout their care.
* **Growth and capacity.** Grow completed visits and procedures by strengthening relationships with referring providers, making it easy to refer patients, and keeping referring offices informed. Convert more referrals into completed visits and procedures through timely scheduling, better use of clinic and ASC capacity, and fewer avoidable cancellations.
* **Stronger financial performance.** Labor and supply costs managed to budget, with timely resolution of operational issues affecting collections.
* **Less manual work and clearer accountability.** Use technology and automation to simplify workflows. Set clear ownership for follow-up and use data to track whether changes improve performance and hold over time.

**Preferred**

* Experience in physician practice management, ambulatory surgery, or another regulated service environment.
* Experience coordinating operations across locations or across teams with distinct professional responsibilities.

**Candidates from outside healthcare are encouraged to apply.** Leadership experience and a record of improving operations are essential. Physician practice management experience is optional.

Benefits:

* 401(k)
* 401(k) matching
* Dental insurance
* Health insurance
* Paid time off
* Vision insurance

Work Location: In person

records.title: Director, Central Laboratory Operations
records.description:
By clicking the “Apply” button, I understand that my employment application process with Takeda will commence and that the information I provide in my application will be processed in line with Takeda’s Privacy Notice and Terms of Use. I further attest that all information I submit in my employment application is true to the best of my knowledge.

**Job Description**
-------------------

OBJECTIVES/PURPOSE

 

* Builds and leads Takeda’s new Central Laboratory Operations group, defining the vision, operating model, organizational design, capabilities, and ways of working required to deliver enterprise technical and operational oversight of central laboratory services across global clinical development programs.
* Establishes the foundational infrastructure for central laboratory oversight, including processes, vendor strategy, systems, and metrics, so that central laboratory solutions are technically sound, operationally executable, globally compliant, and inspection-ready from study design through database lock and study closeout.
* Provides leadership of the Sample Management group, ensuring its in-trial activities interface effectively with central laboratory operations. Biorepository and biobank activities are out of scope for this role.
* Partners with Clinical Science, Clinical Operations, Translational Medicine, Translational Biomarkers and Bioanalytics, Data Management, Biometrics, Regulatory Affairs, Quality, Procurement, and external laboratory providers to deliver consistent, scalable central laboratory capabilities across the portfolio.

ACCOUNTABILITIES

 

**Building the Central Laboratory Operations Group (primary focus)**

* Define and execute the vision, strategy, and multi-year roadmap to stand up the Central Laboratory Operations group, including mission, scope, service model, phased capability build, and measures of success.
* Design the organizational structure, roles, and resourcing plan; recruit, onboard, develop, and lead a high-performing team of central laboratory technical and operational experts.
* Establish the central laboratory operating model and oversight framework, including standards, decision rights (RACI), governance forums, escalation pathways, and interfaces with Clinical Operations, Translational Medicine, Translational Biomarkers and Bioanalytics, Data Management, Biometrics, Quality, and Procurement.
* Develop the foundational processes, SOPs, work instructions, templates, and training needed to standardize central laboratory startup, conduct, and closeout across studies, and transition existing study-level central laboratory activities into the new group without disruption to ongoing studies.
* Develop the business case, budget, and resource forecasts for the group, and secure leadership alignment and sponsorship for the phased build-out.
* Lead the central laboratory vendor strategy, including evaluation, selection, and qualification of central laboratories and will consult in evaluation and selection of specialty laboratories as appropriate, technical capability assessments, quality and compliance reviews, contracting input with Procurement, service-level expectations, KPIs, issue escalation, and ongoing vendor governance.
* Provide technical oversight during clinical development planning and protocol design by assessing laboratory feasibility, test menus, specimen requirements, reference ranges, turnaround times, and the operational impact of study endpoints and schedules.
* Establish central laboratory systems and data capabilities, including laboratory information management systems, electronic data capture interfaces, data transfer specifications, edit checks, result reconciliation, traceability, and data readiness for analysis, database lock, and regulatory submission.
* Build quality and regulatory compliance into the group from inception, including ICH-GCP, applicable GCLP principles, CLIA/CAP or equivalent laboratory requirements, data integrity, inspection readiness, audits, deviations, CAPAs, and vendor change controls. Lead IVDR requirements for each protocol.
* Establish portfolio-level central laboratory metrics, dashboards, and executive reporting for quality, timeliness, cost, risk, capacity, data delivery, and vendor performance; use trends and root-cause analysis to drive risk mitigation and sustained improvement.
* Drive modernization through standardized processes, automation, digital integration, data analytics, and emerging laboratory technologies as the group matures.

**Sample Management Group Oversight**

* Provide leadership of the Sample Management group, including setting priorities, allocating resources, approving goals, and supporting talent development; day-to-day sample management execution remains with the Sample Management lead.
* Define the handoffs between central laboratory operations and sample management (e.g., laboratory manuals, collection kits, sample shipment to central laboratories) so roles, responsibilities, and escalation paths are clear.
* Ensure appropriate sample management resourcing and integration at the study level to ensure end-to-end sample mgmt support during study conduct
* Serve as the senior escalation point for sample-related issues that affect central laboratory testing, study timelines, or data quality.

EDUCATION, EXPERIENCE, COMPETENCIES AND SKILLS

* Bachelor's degree in Life Sciences, Clinical Laboratory Science, Biomedical Science, Pharmacy, or a related field; advanced

degree such as MS, PhD, PharmD, or equivalent is preferred.

* 10+ years of experience in the pharmaceutical, biotechnology, central laboratory, diagnostic laboratory, or other regulated life-

sciences environment, with significant leadership responsibility for global clinical laboratory delivery.

* Proven track record of building a new function, team, or capability from the ground up, including defining strategy, operating

model, organizational design, processes, and governance.

* Demonstrated people leadership experience, including recruiting, developing, and managing teams and overseeing managers in

a matrixed global environment.

* Strong technical knowledge of central and specialty laboratory operations, service models, test menus, analytical platforms,

specimen requirements, reference intervals, laboratory workflow controls, and fit-for-purpose testing within clinical

development.

* Experience selecting, qualifying, contracting with, and governing global central laboratory vendors, including KPI/SLA

management, issue escalation, audits, CAPAs, and continuous improvement.

* Working knowledge of ICH-GCP, applicable GCLP principles, CLIA/CAP or equivalent laboratory standards, IVDR where

applicable, data integrity expectations, and global health authority inspection requirements.

* Strong knowledge of laboratory informatics and clinical technology, including LIMS, laboratory data standards, electronic data

capture interfaces, data transfer specifications, reconciliation, traceability, and data quality controls.

* General familiarity with clinical study sample management sufficient to lead the Sample Management group and manage

interfaces with central laboratory operations.

* Excellent strategic thinking, change leadership, risk management, communication, negotiation, vendor-management, and

executive presentation skills, with the ability to influence senior stakeholders across functions.

**This position is currently classified as “remote” in accordance with Takeda’s Hybrid and Remote Work policy**

**Takeda Compensation and Benefits Summary**

We understand compensation is an important factor as you consider the next step in your career. We are committed to equitable pay for all employees, and we strive to be more transparent with our pay practices.

**For Location:**

Massachusetts - Virtual

**U.S. Base Salary Range:**

$177,000.00 - $278,080.00

The estimated salary range reflects an anticipated range for this position. The actual base salary offered may depend on a variety of factors, including the qualifications of the individual applicant for the position, years of relevant experience, specific and unique skills, level of education attained, certifications or other professional licenses held, and the location in which the applicant lives and/or from which they will be performing the job. The actual base salary offered will be in accordance with state or local minimum wage requirements for the job location.

records.title: Director, Operational Excellence
records.description:
* Team:Industrial Operations & Product Supply
* Location:Saratoga Springs
* Req ID:R53235
* Contract:Full time
* Work Pattern:Onsite

**The role**
------------

**Build our future together:**

At Regeneron, we use science and innovation to develop life-changing medicines for people with serious diseases. We’re hiring an Associate Director/Director of Operational Excellence for our highly automated bulk/ drug substance manufacturing plant, supporting 20–30 tech transfers a year alongside commercial delivery responsibility. GMP production will run concurrently with construction and CQV for 3–5 years. This role requires both building and operating.

 
 

This site operates on a foundation of strategy, execution, and discipline. Every function at the site owns a pyramid of metrics derived from annual goal planning that connects the site’s strategic goals to the factory floor, with performance measured back up to leadership to monitor, track, and mitigate against contingencies quantified using SMART goals in days and dollars.

 
 

The Associate Director/Director of Operational Excellence runs our site MDI (managing for daily improvements) OpEx, continuous improvement programs, and all site PMO operations owning the site project register and deciding how work is staffed and prioritized across the project portfolio while coordinating cross-functional projects. They build the operating rhythm that turns discrete functions into one aligned site team as the site scales to six suites, and owns the site’s strategy, execution, and culture discipline planning. Lead executive-level investigations and special initiatives as project/program lead, absorbing crisis response so operational leaders can stay focused on daily management.

 
 

**When & where:**

* Location: Saratoga Springs, New York, United States

* Work model: Monday-Friday, 8am-4:30pm
 

 

**Discover your role:**

* Run site MDI including ownership of the Tier 6 site critical issue forum, ensuring cross-functional blockers are surfaced and resolved quickly

* Establish and sustain the site's cadence of daily, weekly, and monthly forums so issues are raised and resolved at the right level

* Lead OpEx and continuous improvement programs, building and prioritizing a CI project pipeline and delivering realized savings

* Lead all site PMO activities, owning the site project register and deciding how work is staffed and prioritized across the project portfolio, coordinating cross-functional projects and site initiatives and driving on-time delivery

* Own site strategy, execution, and rigor planning for culture translating strategic priorities into a disciplined, trackable execution plan across the site

* Own MDI and all standard work initiatives site-wide, ensuring consistent methodology and application across every function and suite

* Own site-wide implementation of lean principles building and driving the phased adoption roadmap across leadership, suites, and functions, from initial leadership alignment through daily floor-level practice

* Own site business analytics building and maintaining the reporting, dashboards, and KPI infrastructure that drive MDI, CI prioritization, and Site Leadership Team decision-making

* Co-lead the monthly finance/business review with finance operations, reconciling cost and capital needs against the site's financial plan

* Coach leaders and teams in Lean and problem-solving methods and build an OpEx culture across the site

* Embed MDI and OpEx practices as suites come online so new suites start up with the site's operating standards

* Partner with manufacturing, quality, technical services, technical operations, supply chain, and Finance as a member of the site leadership team

* Embed the digital and connected plant model in site MDI, using real-time data and digital tools for daily management and escalation

* Own the site's multi-year operational efficiency roadmap, driving leaner operations and delivering year-over-year efficiency gains

* Build, coach, and retain a high-performing OpEx team; establish high standards for performance management and accountability; perform other duties as required

records.description:
1.0 FTE Full time Day - 08 Hour R2655441 Hybrid 108400006 SC Administration Business & Administration PALO ALTO, 1840 Embarcadero, California

If you're ready to be part of our legacy of hope and innovation, we encourage you to take the first step and explore our current job openings. Your best is waiting to be discovered.

 
Day - 08 Hour (United States of America)

**This is a Stanford Health Care job.** 
 
**A Brief Overview** 
The Director of Supply Chain Operational Excellence is a senior leadership role driving enterprise‑wide efficiency, innovation, and transformation across a Gartner top‑2 ranked healthcare supply chain. With system‑wide influence and a seat at the leadership table, this role partners closely with the Chief Supply Chain Officer and Vice President of Strategic Initiatives to turn strategy into measurable results. The ideal candidate combines healthcare supply chain expertise with strong program management skills and a passion for developing people, leading change, and delivering measurable, enterprise‑wide impact. 
 
**Locations** 
Stanford Health Care 
 
**What you will do**

* Maintain continuous alignment with defined organizational and departmental strategic business objectives in conjunction with leadership.
* Direct and ensure the efficient operation of day-to-day activities of the team and ensure competency of all staff.
* Supports and partners on Change Management, Training and Communications activities as needed for effective performance improvement and project management.
* Act in an advisory capacity to all Supply Chain divisions, programs, staff and leaders.
* Provide expertise, guidance and training on Performance Improvement and Project Management best practices.
* Apply LEAN/Six Sigma principles and methods to identify waste reduction and performance optimization opportunities across Supply Chain operations.
* Implement, oversee and continuously improve Supply Chain systems, processes and standard work to drive the efficient management of operations across Logistics, Sourcing, Procurement, Business Office, Resiliency, Sustainability, Data Management and other functions.
* Build, develop and grow business relationships with Supply Chain’s key stakeholders and partners including but not limited to the Interventional Platform, A/P, Pharmacy, and IT.
* Lead cross-departmental initiatives, establishing strong governance, communication, and accountability to deliver progress measurable through mutually agreed KPIs.
* Align and collaborate with the enterprise Performance Improvement team and Stanford Operating System (SOS).
* Lead the implementation of programs and/or projects as assigned by the Administrative Director.

**Education Qualifications**

* Requires a Bachelor’s degree in a work-related discipline/field from an accredited college or university.
* Relevant experience in lieu of degree may be considered. Relevant experience in lieu of degree is in addition to the experience requirements for this position.

**Experience Qualifications**

* Seven (7) years of progressively responsible and directly related work experience.

**Required Knowledge, Skills and Abilities**

* Must have strong leadership and interpersonal skills and be effective at people management including the ability to delegate assignments and share decision-making with team members and direct reports as appropriate.
* Excellent communication skills including the ability to present, and to write in a clear and understandable manner.
* Ability to understand complex verbal or written instructions and translate to action to deliver quantitative and qualitative results.
* Must be well organized and systematic, and able to design, implement and maintain standard work processes.
* Knowledge of project management methodologies to lead complex project teams and large scope projects, including managing resources (people, costs, time).
* Familiar with and able to apply Lean Six Sigma concepts and techniques including value stream mapping, kaizen, Five Whys, VoC, RCA etc. for structured process improvement.
* Demonstrated expertise in leading change management initiatives within Agile delivery environments.
* Ability to multi-task and handle multiple priorities while managing aggressive deadlines. Knowledge of Supply Chain functions, practices, and operational challenges.
* Understanding of healthcare and clinical concepts.

**Licenses and Certifications**

* Lean Six Sigma Certification preferred .
* PMP - Project Mgmt Professional preferred .
* CMRP (Certified Materials & Resource Professionals) preferred.

**Physical Demands and Work Conditions** 
**Blood Borne Pathogens**

* Category II - Tasks that involve NO exposure to blood, body fluids or tissues, but employment may require performing unplanned Category I tasks

**These principles apply to ALL employees:** 
 
**SHC Commitment to Providing an Exceptional Patient & Family Experience** 
 
*Stanford Health Care sets a high standard for delivering value and an exceptional experience for our patients and families. Candidates for employment and existing employees must adopt and execute C-I-CARE standards for all of patients, families and towards each other. C-I-CARE is the foundation of Stanford’s patient-experience and represents a framework for patient-centered interactions. Simply put, we do what it takes to enable and empower patients and families to focus on health, healing and recovery.* 
 
*You will do this by executing against our three experience pillars, from the patient and family’s perspective:*

* Know Me: Anticipate my needs and status to deliver effective care
* Show Me the Way: Guide and prompt my actions to arrive at better outcomes and better health
* Coordinate for Me: Own the complexity of my care through coordination

**Equal Opportunity Employer Stanford Health Care (SHC) strongly values diversity and is committed to equal opportunity and non-discrimination in****all of****its policies and practices, including the area of employment. Accordingly, SHC does not discriminate against any person on the basis of race, color, sex, sexual orientation or gender identity and/or expression, religion, age, national or ethnic origin, political beliefs, marital status, medical condition, genetic information, veteran status, or disability, or the perception of any of the above. People of all genders, members of all racial and ethnic groups, people with disabilities, and veterans are encouraged to apply. Qualified applicants with criminal convictions will be considered after an individualized assessment of the conviction and the job requirements.**

Base Pay Scale: Generally starting at $81.59 - $108.12 per hour

The salary of the finalist selected for this role will be set based on a variety of factors, including but not limited to, internal equity, experience, education, specialty and training. This pay scale is not a promise of a particular wage.

records.description:
**What makes DHL great?** Our People! We know each employee’s individual contributions make us the #1 Express Delivery and Logistics Company in the world.

***Distinguished as No. 1 World’s Best Workplace™ by Great Place to Work and Fortune Magazine***

DHL Express is committed to maintaining an environment that empowers every team member to make the greatest possible impact on our business. Our culture is about personal commitment – to our business, to each other and to our global communities. DHL is dedicated to being a great place to work. In addition to competitive compensation packages, our employees enjoy a range of programs, services and benefits that bring the best to their personal lives.

**Start YOUR career with DHL today…**

The **Sr. Director Operations** is responsible for providing strategic input and leading the implementation of the Courier and Pick-up & Delivery strategy. This role ensures the safe, secure, timely, and accurate transportation and delivery of mail, parcels, small packages, and legal documents between locations, in alignment with business objectives, operational requirements, corporate guidelines, and policies.

**Key Accountabilities:**

* Provide input to develop Couriers, Pick-up & Delivery operations strategy to deliver effective collection, transportation, and delivery of parcels while maintaining exceptional service quality and customer satisfaction.
* Plan, organize and control preparation of annual business plans, operational budgets, workforce planning, and resource allocation for delivery operations.
* Provide expertise, coaching, and leadership to frontline managers and supervisors to ensure execution of daily operational activities, achievement of performance targets, and development of future leaders.
* Manage and control service point operations to enable efficient collection, handling, and distribution of shipments while maintaining compliance with operational standards.
* Manage and control scheduling of transportation capacity, traffic volumes, route structures, and delivery resources to maximize productivity and service performance.
* Lead a workforce of more than 1,000 employees across multiple facilities, fostering a culture of accountability, engagement, safety, and operational excellence.
* Demonstrate strong knowledge and experience operating in unionized environments, including labor relations, contract interpretation, grievance resolution, workforce planning, and effective collaboration with union leadership.
* Oversee large independent contractor (IC) networks and transportation providers, ensuring contractual compliance, operational performance, cost management, and service reliability.
* Drive operational expense (OPEX) management through disciplined financial oversight, productivity initiatives, route optimization, and continuous improvement programs to achieve profitability objectives.
* Partner closely with Network Operations, Gateway Operations, Brokerage, Customs, Aviation, and Commercial teams to ensure seamless execution of customer commitments and network requirements.
* Deploy structured approaches to manage operational procedures including shipment processing, sorting, loading/unloading, documentation, scanning compliance, manifests, secure handling, and custody control.
* Implement reporting standards, performance metrics, and operational dashboards to provide visibility into service performance, cost drivers, productivity, and customer experience measures.
* Anticipate changes in customer demand, economic conditions, labor markets, and transportation trends to proactively adjust operational strategies and resource requirements.
* Identify opportunities to improve transportation, delivery, and customer service solutions through process redesign, technology implementation, and network optimization.
* Monitor operational performance and implement continuous improvement initiatives focused on service quality, productivity, safety, employee engagement, and cost control.
* Lead multiple delivery bases and service centers across geographically diverse markets, ensuring consistent execution of operational standards and business objectives.
* Champion safety, security, and compliance programs while maintaining adherence to company policies, regulatory requirements, and industry best practices.
* Build strong relationships with key customers, local business leaders, and internal stakeholders to support growth initiatives and enhance the overall customer experience.
* Drive organizational change initiatives, workforce transformation efforts, and strategic projects across the region while maintaining high levels of employee engagement and operational performance.

**Skills/Qualifications:**

* Bachelor’s degree required.
* 8+ years of experience in operations and leadership roles.
* Demonstrated experience in budgetary management and financial accountability.
* Strong background in business and operations management, including managing complex operational environments.
* Experience leading courier, Pick-up & Delivery, dock, and transportation operations.
* Proven ability to lead change management and operational improvement initiatives.
* Strong strategic planning and execution capabilities.
* Demonstrated experience in stakeholder management and cross-functional collaboration.
* Proven leadership experience managing a department or business unit comprising multiple teams, including Managers and/or Team Leaders.
* Strong ability to lead, develop, and influence leaders and teams to achieve business and operational objectives.
* Experience establishing priorities, managing resources, and driving performance across multiple operational functions.
* Demonstrated ability to drive employee engagement, foster an inclusive and high-performing culture, and develop strategies that strengthen employee experience, retention, and organizational effectiveness.

**Employee Benefits & Incentives**

DHL Express benefits and incentive offerings are designed to reflect a substantial experience for both employees and their dependents during their career and life journey. The specifics will vary, but wherever you join and in whatever role, you'll find our benefits and rewards are among the best in the industry They include:

* Competitive Pay - Salary Range New Jersey $187,950- $250,600
* Bonus/Incentive Programs
* Retirement Savings – 401K with company match
* Medical, Dental, Vision, well-being programs
* Tuition Reimbursement
* Generous Paid Time Off – Starting at 4 Weeks (PT/FT)
* Paid Leave
* Employee Discount Program
* Employee Assistance & Work Life Program
* Outstanding training opportunities

*DHL is an equal opportunity employer. We evaluate qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, veteran status,* *or any other protected characteristic. The EEO is the Law poster is available here:* *https://www.eeoc.gov/employers/eeo-law-poster*

records.title: Executive Director, Research Administration Transformation & Operational Excellence
records.description:
Discover Your Career at Emory University: Emory University is a leading research university that fosters excellence and attracts world-class talent to innovate today and prepare leaders for the future. We welcome candidates who can contribute to the excellence of our academic community. Description:

The Executive Director for Research Administration Transformation & Operational Excellence provides executive strategic and operational leadership for the Office of Research Administration's (ORA) enterprise-wide transformation portfolio.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:

* Leads an enterprise-wide transformation portfolio spanning research administration functions across schools, units, and Emory Healthcare, requiring university-wide change leadership and executive influence.
* Partners with Artificial Intelligence & Digital Strategy (AI & DS) to implement a broad portfolio that includes enterprise technology implementation (including the Insight grants management system), organizational redesign, shared services transformation, operational performance improvement, artificial intelligence and emerging technology strategy, and research administration training and professional development.
* Directs implementation, ongoing maintenance, and optimization of enterprise systems and tools, including Insight and LegalSifter, and ensures that technology investments support the future-state operating model.
* Co-leads implementation and ongoing review of future-state operating model, including organizational design, workflow refinement, shared services transformation, and operational performance.
* Exercises decision-making authority over implementation, configuration alignment, workflow and business process design, user acceptance, vendor management, future-state operating model alignment, and continuous refinement across pre-award, post-award, agreements, effort reporting, personnel, and compliance modules.
* Manages vendor performance (including Huron), monitors project milestones, and reports status, risks, decisions, and outcomes to the Vice President and Steering Committee.
* Holds executive accountability for realization of transformation outcomes, including organizational effectiveness, service excellence, operational efficiency, adoption, and sustained performance improvement.
* Partners with AI & DS to implement technology programs and enabling capabilities required for responsible AI success. This includes project management, development and evaluation of workflows, tool evaluation, implementation, governance, workforce readiness, and adoption. Manages technology evaluation, implementation, and security coordination in partnership with Emory OIT and Information Security.
* Serves as ORA's operational technologies (Insight, SciShield, Huron, etc.) liaison to central technology and governance bodies.
* Provides subject matter expertise to the Learning and Organizational Development team for the design and deployment of a scalable, role-based training ecosystem that includes Insight and Compass system training, process-compliance content, change enablement, and professional development for ORA and school-based research administration staff.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:

* Bachelor's degree in business administration, public administration, health administration, or a related field from an accredited institution and eight years of progressively responsible professional experience in related research administration experience, including a minimum of five years of experience in a management role with direct supervisory responsibility.
* Master's degree (MBA, MPA, MHA, MS, or related discipline) strongly preferred.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

* Master's degree or doctoral degree in a relevant field.
* Experience with Huron's Insight platform at an R1 university or academic medical center in a project leadership or system administration capacity.
* Direct, client-side experience supporting or co-leading a management consulting engagement (EY, Huron Consulting, Deloitte, or equivalent) in a research or academic operations context.
* Experience building or leading a training, learning and development, or organizational capability function in a higher education or healthcare research environment.
* Knowledge of AI governance frameworks, responsible AI principles, and federal data security and research security requirements.
* Demonstrated experience with process improvement methodologies (Lean, Six Sigma, Agile, or equivalent); certification preferred.
* Professional certification in one or more of the following: research administration (CRA or CPRA), project management (PMP), or change management (Prosci ADKAR / CCMP).
* Experience in a centralized or shared services research administration environment, particularly at an institution transitioning from a decentralized model.
* Familiarity with Emory University's systems, culture, and governance structure, or comparable experience at an AAU or Carnegie R1 institution.

NOTE: Position tasks are generally required to be performed in-person at an Emory University location. Remote work from home day options may be granted at department discretion. Emory reserves the right to change remote work status with notice to employee.

#LI-MR1

Additional Details: Emory is an equal opportunity employer, and qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, protected veteran status or other characteristics protected by state or federal law. Emory University does not discriminate in admissions, educational programs, or employment, including recruitment, hiring, promotions, transfers, discipline, terminations, wage and salary administration, benefits, and training. Students, faculty, and staff are assured of participation in university programs and in the use of facilities without such discrimination. Emory University complies with Section 503 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, the Vietnam Era Veteran's Readjustment Assistance Act, and applicable executive orders, federal and state regulations regarding nondiscrimination, equal opportunity, and affirmative action (for protected veterans and individuals with disabilities). Inquiries regarding this policy should be directed to the Emory University Department of Equity and Civil Rights Compliance, 201 Dowman Drive, Administration Building, Atlanta, GA 30322. Telephone: 404-727-9867 (V) | 404-712-2049 (TDD).
 
 
Emory University is committed to ensuring equal access and providing reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with disabilities upon request. To request this document in an alternate format or to seek a reasonable accommodation, please contact the Department of Accessibility Services at accessibility@emory.edu or call 404-727-9877 (Voice) | 404-712-2049 (TDD). We kindly ask that requests be made at least seven business days in advance to allow adequate time for coordination.

Job Description
 
 
Director, U.S. Vaccines & Infectious Diseases Strategy & Operations
 
 
Position Description
 
 
The Director, U.S. Vaccines & Infectious Diseases Strategy & Operations is a key leadership role responsible for shaping and advancing the strategic and operational priorities of the U.S. Vaccines & Infectious Diseases Business Unit.
 
Reporting directly to the SVP, U.S. Vaccines & Infectious Diseases, this individual will serve as a strategic thought partner to the SVP and Leadership Team, translating business strategy into action, driving alignment across priorities, and enabling disciplined execution. The role requires a strong balance of strategic thinking, operational excellence, influence, and change leadership, with the ability to navigate ambiguity, connect across the organization, and accelerate progress against the BU's most important priorities.
 
 
**Key Responsibilities:** 

* Lead the BU strategic planning and operating process, including annual priority setting, Trimester planning and tracking, and ongoing assessment of progress against key objectives.
* Partner with the SVP and Leadership Team to translate strategy into action, identifying priorities, surfacing opportunities and risks, and driving alignment and accountability across the organization.
* Lead high-priority, cross-functional initiatives that advance BU strategy, transformation, and organizational capabilities, including evolving commercial capabilities, new ways of working, AI, and other emerging business priorities.
* Drive leadership effectiveness and decision-making by shaping and facilitating Leadership Team meetings, leader forums, strategic planning sessions, and other key business forums that enable alignment and action.
* Shape BU communications and engagement strategy, ensuring business priorities, strategic direction, and key messages are translated into clear and compelling communications across the organization, including Town Halls and other leadership forums.
* Partner with Leadership Team sponsors to advance talent, culture, and organizational priorities, including Talent & Culture working groups, employee development initiatives, and efforts to strengthen organizational capability and engagement.
* Partner across key financial planning processes, including forecasting, Profit Plan, and investor relations connecting strategic priorities with financial considerations and partnering across Finance and business stakeholders to enable informed decision-making.
* Identify opportunities to strengthen BU effectiveness, simplify ways of working, build organizational capabilities, and accelerate execution of strategic priorities.

**Required Experience:** 

* Bachelor's degree required.
* Minimum of 5 years of experience in marketing, sales, market access, strategy and operations, marketing support, within the pharmaceutical or biotechnology industry.
* Strong strategic thinking, problem-solving, and decision-making capabilities, including the ability to assess complex business challenges, identify strategic choices, and develop clear recommendations.
* Proven ability to influence and lead without direct authority across complex, matrixed organizations.
* Demonstrated ability to influence senior leaders, with the courage to challenge thinking, bring an independent point of view, and constructively navigate differing perspectives.
* Ability to navigate ambiguity and evolving priorities, quickly create structure from white space, and move work forward with sound judgment and learning agility.
* Demonstrated ability to prioritize competing demands, maintain focus on the highest-impact work, and align teams around clear priorities.
* Ability to inspire, motivate, mentor, and align others around a shared vision and clear priorities, with or without direct reporting relationships.
* Strong balance of strategic orientation and operational discipline, with the ability to move seamlessly between long-term priorities and near-term execution.
* Demonstrated ability to connect insights and priorities across functions and levels of the organization, bringing an enterprise perspective while maintaining focus on BU objectives.

**Preferred Experience and Skills:** 

* Vaccines and/or Infectious Diseases experience.
* Experience supporting or leading strategy and operations within a complex commercial organization.
* Experience leading enterprise or cross-functional transformation, capability-building, or change initiatives.
