**About CAMP Systems:**
At CAMP Systems, we are the trusted leader in aircraft compliance and health management, proudly serving the global business aviation industry. With over 20,000 aircraft and 33,000 engines supported on our cutting-edge platforms, and partnerships with more than 1,300 maintenance facilities and parts suppliers worldwide, we’re shaping the future of aviation technology. Since our founding in 1968, we’ve grown to a dynamic team of 1,600+ employees across 14 locations globally—all united by a passion for innovation and excellence.

**Our Mission & Vision:**
We connect the aviation industry through smart technology to make flight safer and more efficient, driving the future of aviation with intelligence and exceptional customer experiences.

**Our Values & Excellence Mindset:**
We are customer obsessed, trust-driven, owners of our work, stronger together, constantly curious, and boldly innovative.

**What You Will Experience in This Role:**

The Director - Quality Assurance drives quality across CAMP's Aircraft Health Management business and provides quality oversight for data and process quality concerns. The role owns the QMS, the internal audit program, and the full quality escape lifecycle, and serves as CAMP's quality voice with OEMs, regulators, and key customers. The right candidate combines deep aviation maintenance knowledge with a disciplined, data-driven approach to compliance and continuous improvement.

This is a high-visibility leadership role reporting to the Vice President, Aviation Health Management Operations. The Director partners with senior leaders across a global organization and will build on an established quality program: strengthening the QMS, deepening OEM and customer confidence, and scaling quality practices as AHM grows.

**Responsibilities:**

**Strategy & Leadership**

* Own and lead quality strategy across the full Aircraft Health Management organization, spanning maintenance tracking and engine health monitoring services, aligned with CAMP's business objectives.
* Serve as the escalation point for quality complaints from customer-facing, maintenance compliance, engine health monitoring, flight scheduling, and inventory functions.
* Partner with senior management and departmental leaders to embed quality methodologies across the organization and lead the associated change management.
* Own the quality budget, resource plan, and tooling (QMS, audit, and corrective action platforms), and build the succession pipeline for the quality team.

**Quality Management System & Certification**

* Own the Quality Management System (QMS) and quality SOPs, driving continuous improvement and ensuring processes meet strict regulatory and OEM requirements.
* Maintain ISO 9001 (or higher) certification for the engine health monitoring business, serving as external certification audit lead and ensuring ongoing audit readiness.
* Lead QMS management review with executive leadership, setting risk-based quality objectives and ensuring consistent QMS implementation (document control, competency records, data integrity) across all AHM locations in North America, Europe, and India.

**Audit & Compliance**

* Own the internal audit program end to end, including audit planning, execution, reporting, and the selection, training, and management of internal auditors.
* Host and manage OEM, customer, and third-party audits, driving findings to timely closure.

**Quality Escapes & Corrective Action**

* Manage all quality escapes from intake through investigation, root cause analysis, corrective and preventive action, and verification of effectiveness, with clear accountability to customers and OEM partners.
* Define and report corrective action performance metrics (e.g., escape rate, time to containment, on-time closure, recurrence) with clear thresholds and escalation paths.

**OEM & Customer Engagement**

* Facilitate and chair weekly, monthly, and quarterly strategic OEM meetings covering quality trends, KPI compliance, and corrective action status.
* Serve as primary quality liaison to OEM partners, regulatory bodies, and high-profile customers and large fleet operators under significant OEM contracts.
* Facilitate weekly, monthly, and quarterly quality reviews with senior management and functional leaders, translating escape, audit, and customer feedback data into trends and strategic quality initiatives.

**Continuous Improvement & Team Leadership**

* Lead process improvement using Lean Six Sigma methods, mentoring teams and driving measurable reductions in escapes, rework, and risk.
* Maintain an executive quality scorecard (customer feedback, escapes, audit results, corrective action performance) to drive data-based decisions.
* Lead, mentor, and develop a team of four, setting priorities and fostering a culture of excellence, accountability, and collaboration.
* Partner with AHM operations, training, and product leaders to ensure analyst competency, training effectiveness, and quality readiness for new products, processes, and teams.

**You have:**

* Bachelor's degree in Aerospace, Engineering, Quality Management, or a related field; advanced degree a plus.
* Minimum of 10 years of proven leadership experience in the aviation or aerospace sector, with senior quality assurance experience preferred.
* Strong working knowledge of aviation maintenance and its regulatory requirements (FAA, EASA, and OEM requirements). Hands-on aviation maintenance experience may offset formal credentials.
* Experience managing quality escapes, investigations, root cause analysis, and corrective action programs.
* Experience owning or managing a QMS in a regulated environment, with working knowledge of ISO 9001 (AS9100 familiarity a plus).
* Strong analytical skills, with the ability to turn quality data into executive-level metrics, insights, and recommendations.
* Excellent communication, negotiation, and presentation skills, with the ability to build relationships with OEMs, customers, and leaders at all levels of the organization.
* Strategic thinking with a strong focus on results and the ability to manage complex projects and initiatives.
* Ability to lead across a multi-site, multi-region team; willingness to travel to CAMP offices, OEM, and customer sites as needed.

**Nice to have:**

* Certified ISO 9001 Internal/External Auditor (or equivalent lead auditor certification) with hands-on audit experience.
* Six Sigma Black Belt, with demonstrated process improvement results.
* Quality manager certification (e.g., ASQ CQM) or Certified Quality Auditor (CQA) is a bonus.
* Experience working with large OEM contracts and high-profile customers or large fleet operators.
* Experience in aircraft maintenance tracking, engine trend monitoring, or other SaaS/data-driven service environments.

**Why Work at CAMP?**

Join a culture where your ideas matter, your impact is real, and your growth is supported. Be part of a team reimagining the future of aviation.

**Overview**
Resonetics is a global leader in advanced engineering, prototyping, product development, and micro manufacturing, driving innovation in the medical device industry. With rapid expansion across all our locations, we continue to push the boundaries of technology while fostering a dynamic, employee-centered culture. Our commitment to excellence and continuous improvement makes Resonetics an exciting place for professionals passionate about shaping the future of micro-manufacturing and being part of something bigger
  
  
The Quality Director plays a pivotal role in leading and strengthening operational quality and quality compliance within a large-scale contract manufacturing facility. Responsible for both Product Quality and Quality Management System (QMS) compliance, this leader ensures quality operations within the manufacturing environment consistently meet customer, regulatory, and business expectations.
  
  
This individual combines strategic vision with hands-on operational quality leadership, ensuring Resonetics delivers world-class quality in a fast-paced, highly regulated medical device manufacturing environment. The role demands proven experience within manufacturing operations, deep expertise in ISO 13485 and 21 CFR Part 820, mastery of advanced quality assurance techniques, and the ability to align and elevate quality performance across multiple value streams.
  
  
Join Resonetics and be part of a team that’s redefining medical device manufacturing. If you’re passionate about innovation and thrive in a fast-paced environment, we’d love to hear from you.

**Operational Quality Leadership**

* Own and lead all aspects of manufacturing quality performance, ensuring operational processes deliver consistent, compliant, and high-yield outcomes.
* Partner closely with Operations leadership to embed quality into daily production activities and drive problem-solving directly on the manufacturing floor.
* Implement and oversee statistical process control (SPC), process capability, and other data-driven tools to ensure process stability and continuous improvement.
* Monitor and manage critical quality metrics, taking immediate action to address gaps and prevent recurrence of issues.
* Oversee validation strategies (IQ/OQ/PQ) for manufacturing processes and equipment, ensuring robustness and compliance.
* Provide quality leadership in New Product Introduction (NPI), ensuring robust process validation, risk management, and seamless transition from development into full-scale manufacturing.

**Quality Systems & Compliance**

* Ensure the ISO-certified QMS is operationally effective within manufacturing sites and continuously improved to support business growth.
* Maintain full compliance with ISO 13485, 21 CFR Part 820, and other relevant standards through proactive system management and audit readiness.

**Continuous Improvement & Problem Solving**

* Lead root cause investigations and corrective actions for complex production challenges.
* Drive Lean and Six Sigma initiatives that enhance manufacturing efficiency while strengthening compliance and product quality.
* Share best practices across sites to ensure standardization and scalability of quality improvements.

**Customer & Supplier Interface**

* Serve as the primary quality leader for high-visibility customers, ensuring confidence in Resonetics’ ability to deliver consistently high-quality products.
* Lead the supplier quality program, ensuring raw materials and outsourced processes meet stringent requirements to support operational excellence.

**Team Leadership & Development**

* Build and mentor a strong quality team embedded within the manufacturing organization.
* Provide training in advanced quality tools (Gage R&R, SPC, pFMEA, Risk Analysis, Validation, Root Cause Analysis, CAPA) to elevate operational capability.
* Foster a culture of quality culture and ownership on the production floor, engaging all levels of the workforce.

**Required Qualifications**

* Minimum 7 years’ experience in a Medical Device Quality Management role.
* Lean and/or Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt
* Demonstrated background in an ISO 13485 and 21 CFR 820 quality management system.
* Strong communication skills (verbal and writing)
* BS degree in a management or engineering discipline
* Experience hosting FDA inspections and ISO audits

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Prior experience in a technical, regulated environment.
* Experience with finished medical device assembly and oversight of sterilization
* Experience with Quality Management Software (eQMS) and ERP systems
* Certified Quality Auditor

* Light office work, approximately 25%+ travel

The compensation for this role is competitive and will be based on experience and qualifications. The anticipated range is $144,000.00 - $222,000.00.

**Job Title**
- Executive Director, Quality Assurance
  
  
**Department**
- Quality Assurance
  
  
**Work Location**
- Cranbury NJ (On-site)
  
  
Position Summary
  
  
The Head of U.S. Quality provides strategic, scientific, and operational leadership for Quality Assurance and Quality Control across U.S. operations. The role is accountable for maintaining an effective, risk-based Quality Management System and ensuring that research, development, clinical, CMC, and manufacturing activities comply with applicable global regulations, industry standards, company policies, and client expectations. The position drives quality excellence, inspection readiness, organizational capability, and continuous improvement, with particular emphasis on biologics, commercial manufacturing, and complex CDMO operations.
  
  
Key Responsibilities
  
  
Strategic Quality Leadership
  
  

* Provide strategic and scientific leadership for the U.S. quality organization and execute the global Quality strategy in alignment with company standards, policies, and business objectives.
* Lead Quality Assurance and Quality Control functions supporting R&D, Clinical, CMC, technology transfer, manufacturing, and commercial operations.
* Embed quality considerations into strategic planning, new services, product development, site improvement, and organizational growth decisions.
* Serve as the senior Quality representative with clients, partners, regulatory authorities, external auditors, and industry forums.

Quality Management System and Compliance
  
  

* Establish, govern, monitor, and continuously improve a robust, risk-based Quality Management System and related procedural framework.
* Provide oversight of change control, deviations, investigations, CAPA, quality risk management, document control, training, validation, data trending, and management review.
* Ensure controlled documentation, including SOPs, master and executed batch records, validation protocols and reports, and technical reports, is accurate, current, and compliant.
* Identify and implement systemic improvements based on compliance trends, quality metrics, inspection outcomes, industry benchmarks, and emerging regulatory expectations.

Regulatory and Inspection Readiness
  
  

* Ensure ongoing compliance with applicable GxP and cGMP requirements, including FDA, EMA, NMPA/CFDA, ICH, USP, EP, and Chinese Pharmacopoeia expectations where applicable.
* Lead regulatory inspections and client audits, including inspection preparation, health-authority interactions, response strategy, remediation, and effectiveness monitoring.
* Maintain current knowledge of global regulatory requirements, industry trends, and best practices, and translate changes into timely updates to systems, procedures, and training.

Quality Assurance and Product Disposition
  
  

* Provide leadership and direction for QA oversight of manufacturing and laboratory operations, including batch record review, product disposition, quality events, and release decisions.
* Oversee review and approval of critical quality and technical documentation and ensure quality decisions are scientifically sound, risk-based, timely, and well documented.
* Facilitate quality risk assessments and mitigation plans to anticipate and address potential product, process, compliance, and supply risks.

Quality Control and Laboratory Governance
  
  

* Ensure Quality Control laboratories are appropriately equipped, staffed, and governed to support in-process, release, stability, and other required testing.
* Oversee analytical method development, qualification/validation, transfer, lifecycle management, laboratory investigations, and data integrity controls.
* Use laboratory and environmental monitoring trends, KPIs, and leading indicators to inform risk management, resource allocation, and improvement priorities.

Supplier, Material, and Client Quality
  
  

* Oversee supplier qualification, material quality, quality agreements, and the quality governance of raw materials and components used in manufacturing.
* Lead quality-related client communications, support client governance, participate in audits, and ensure observations and commitments are addressed effectively.
* Build trusted relationships with internal and external stakeholders while protecting compliance, product quality, patient safety, and client satisfaction.

Operational Excellence and Cross-functional Partnership
  
  

* Drive continuous improvement and operational excellence across Quality operations using data, trends, metrics, and appropriate problem-solving methodologies.
* Partner with Manufacturing, R&D, CMC, Clinical, Engineering, Supply Chain, Regulatory Affairs, and other functions to resolve complex quality issues and sustain compliant operations.
* Provide cross-functional support to ensure the sustainability and continual improvement of quality and compliance systems across the organization.

People, Organization, and Financial Leadership
  
  

* Build, recruit, lead, and develop a high-performing, diverse Quality organization with clear accountabilities, succession plans, and capability-development priorities.
* Manage the employee lifecycle for direct reports, including selection, hiring, onboarding, goal setting, coaching, development, performance discussions, and recognition.
* Establish meaningful quality performance metrics and regularly evaluate organizational effectiveness, capacity, and capability against business needs.
* Prepare and manage the Quality budget and expenditures, and support capital expenditure requests for quality, laboratory, site improvement, and renovation needs.

**Minimum Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree or higher in Chemistry, Biochemistry, Biology, Pharmaceutical Sciences, Biological Engineering, or a related scientific or engineering field; an advanced degree is preferred.
* At least 15 years of experience in the pharmaceutical or biotechnology industry, including at least 10 years in Quality leadership or Quality management roles.
* Extensive experience in a GMP-regulated biopharmaceutical, biologics, or CDMO environment; experience with antibody-drug conjugates is highly desirable.
* Demonstrated commercial manufacturing experience and broad knowledge of R&D QA, GLP, Clinical, CMC, Manufacturing QA, and QC environments.
* Proven experience leading cross-functional Quality organizations in complex, multi-site, or international settings.
* Deep knowledge of global GxP regulations, Quality Management Systems, regulatory inspections, and compliance frameworks.
* Experience interacting directly with regulatory authorities, clients, auditors, and strategic partners.
* Proven ability to lead large-scale programs, organizational change, quality improvement initiatives, and inspection remediation.

Leadership Competencies and Skills
  
  

* Strategic and systems thinking with the ability to connect quality risk, regulatory expectations, operational performance, and business priorities.
* Strong people leadership, organization-building, coaching, succession planning, and change-management capability.
* Excellent communication, influencing, negotiation, and stakeholder-management skills at executive, client, and regulatory levels.
* Strong analytical, statistical, problem-solving, and decision-making skills for complex and ambiguous quality issues.
* Demonstrated commitment to quality culture, data integrity, scientific rigor, patient safety, and continuous improvement.
* Ability to operate effectively across cultures, functions, sites, and global time zones.

Physical and Travel Requirements
  
  
The role may require occasional domestic and international travel to support client meetings, regulatory inspections, conferences, partner interactions, and oversight of external or multi-site quality activities.
  
  
Role Success Measures
  
  

* An effective, sustainable, and inspection-ready Quality Management System.
* Consistent regulatory compliance and timely closure of audit, inspection, and quality commitments.
* Robust product disposition, laboratory, supplier, and quality-event governance.
* Data-driven continuous improvement and measurable reduction of recurring quality risks.
* A capable, engaged, and accountable Quality organization aligned with U.S. and global business needs.
* Strong, transparent, and trusted relationships with clients, regulators, partners, and internal stakeholders.

**The salary range for this position is $193,000 - $329,000**
**An Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, or protected veteran status and will not be discriminated against on the basis of disability**

records.title: Vice President, Global GMP Quality
records.description:
**MISSION**

Mirum Pharmaceuticals is a biopharmaceutical company dedicated to transforming the treatment of rare diseases. We are passionate about advancing scientific discoveries to become important medicines for rare disease patients. We are collaborative, creative, and experienced professionals and we’re looking to augment our team with other individuals who embody our values: care, be real, get it done, and have fun, seriously.

**POSITION SUMMARY**

The VP, Global GMP Quality position will be responsible for leading the GMP quality functional teams at Mirum and its subsidiaries (US and International). This position will play a pivotal role in steering the organization toward an ongoing commitment to quality improvement, driving efforts to identify areas for optimization, innovation, and excellence. This person will be responsible for managing, mentoring and supporting a GMP Operations team of clinical and commercial Quality Assurance (QA) and Quality Control (QC) professionals. This person will provide leadership and hands-on support to ensure the seamless execution of GMP QA and QC functions, including product quality complaint investigation, root-cause investigations, and the reporting of critical GMP issues to executive management.  This person will also be responsible for leading, providing direction, resources, and guidance to ensure that all GMP quality processes are executed with the highest standards of compliance with FDA, EMA, and other international regulatory requirements, corporate objectives, and industry best practices. This role also involves ensuring that the GMP and GDP quality functions are closely aligned with the organization’s broader strategic goals, guaranteeing that quality initiatives support the company’s mission, vision, and operational objectives.

**JOB FUNCTIONS/RESPONSIBILITIES**

* Serve as the GMP quality strategic leader to assist the head of quality to further develop the quality culture at Mirum to be compliant, collaborative and phase appropriate.
* Develop and execute a global GMP quality strategy to align with corporate goals and regulatory requirements.
* Serve as the GMP quality strategic leader within the Quality group to lead the GMP QA and QC functional teams in fostering professional development and guiding staff in all aspects of GMP/GDP competence in meeting domestic and international regulatory requirements and guidelines (FDA, EMA, MHRA, NMPA, ICH, etc.).
* Lead the development and optimization of key processes, functional collaboration, transformational initiatives, and operational excellence through the GMP/GDP Quality Unit.
* Serve as the GMP quality lead in Audits and Regulatory Inspections in providing strategic leadership, interactions, responses, CAPA plans and implementation.
* Lead the GMP inspection readiness for the Company including GMP Quality improvement and maintenance.
* Host/Manage GMP PAI/PLI inspections at Mirum and support Mirum PAI/PLI related CMO inspections.
* Drive corporate values, vision, goals, and objectives through collaboration with senior leaders building cross-functional networks to influence operational capabilities.
* Serve as a GMP Quality advisor to cross-functional stakeholders within Mirum global organizations and subsidiaries.
* Promote collaboration across internal and external functional teams and stakeholders to identify, design and implement opportunities for improvement across all areas of GMP and GDP quality responsibilities.
* Establish, maintain, and ensure effectiveness of GMP and GDP quality programs and documentation to assure GxP compliance in the domestic and international regulatory environment.
* Oversee, support and perform all aspects of GMP QA and QC activities and functions for drug manufacturing to ensure product quality and supply chain integrity.
* Oversee and support all aspects of clinical and commercial product release which includes direct to market, partner and distributor.
* Serve as the Material Review Board (MRB) chair-person designee.
* Develop and execute a global recall strategy that integrates domestic and international recalls.
* Serve as the Recall Coordinator in the recall committee and support the recall/mock recall process.
* Collaborate with Commercial Organization on launch strategies, NPP/EAP/CUP programs and provide input as a Quality SME.
* Review and approval of GMP, GDP, Partner and Distributor Quality/Technical Agreements.
* Oversee the review and approval of APQR generation in a timely fashion.
* Assess the outcome of GMP audits at CMOs, CTLs, Partners, etc. for a holistic view and to partner with the Technical Operations team in driving improvements.
* Provide strategic and managerial leadership related to company objectives & initiatives and changing regulatory requirements to build, manage, and mentor high-performance QA and QC teams in a global environment.
* Oversee product launch, manufacturing, and distribution quality processes.
* Lead a culture of quality excellence, compliance, and continuous improvement across the organization.
* Ensure global GMP Quality Team meets stakeholder needs, focusing on efficiency, quality, budget management, and corporate growth.
* Serve as Quality Head designee for other GXP areas beyond GMP and GDP as required.
* Requires 15% domestic and international travel, at minimum.

**QUALIFICATIONS**

**Education /Experience:**

* Bachelor’s degree in biochemistry, chemistry, biology, or other science related field (Advanced degree preferred).
* 15+ years of progressive Quality Assurance experience in pharmaceutical and/or Biotech industries, with at least 10+ years in quality leadership role and/or people management including direct & indirect reports.
* Demonstrates extensive knowledge of cGMP manufacturing and Quality Management in compliance with FDA (CBER and/or CDER) and EMA requirements for global-regulated products.
* Demonstrates extensive knowledge of the development and commercialization of medical device in compliance with FDA 21CFR820, ISO13485 and EMA MDR regulations
* Comprehensive knowledge of GMP, GDP, ISO, ICH, and global regulatory requirements.
* Product lifecycle including Late-stage drug development, Regulatory (NDA, MAA, BLA, etc) submission and commercial manufacturing experience.
* Experience with hosting and preparing for inspection readiness and an ability to provide recommendations for its continuous improvement.
* Must be able to work cross functionally as a strong collaborator with ability to partner with internal and external stakeholders across multiple global regions.
* Experience with managing Product Quality Complaints and Pharmacovigilance Quality is a plus
* Experience in rare disease and/or biologics, a plus.

**Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:**

* Extensive hands-on experience in product lifecycle management including late-phase innovative drug development, medical device, combination product and global commercial launch with global CMC regulatory filings (IND/IMPD/CTA/NDA/BLA/MAA, etc.) in a multinational pharmaceutical organization.
* Demonstrate project and cross-functional team leadership, as well as people management skills across different cultures.
* Thorough understanding and working experience in innovative drug development and manufacturing of drugs and biologics concerning GMP operations, quality systems, ICH guidelines, FDA, EMA, and associated international regulatory requirements.
* Extensive working experience with management and oversight of the analytical activities at CDMOs or CTLs with quality mind-set and leadership.
* Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with strategic and sound technically driven decision-making ability.
* Highly effective and strong ability to influence and lead cross-functional teams.
* Strong sense of ethics and honesty.
* Ability to communicate with all levels of management and peers within the organization.
* Effective written and verbal communication skills and interpersonal skills.

The salary range for this position is $320,000 to $340,000 USD. Compensation will be determined based on several factors including, but not limited to; skill set, years of experience, and the employee’s geographic location. Please note that the required compensation details listed in US role postings reflect the base salary only, and do not include bonus, equity, or benefits unless otherwise provided.

**Head of Quality/QA USA**

Ypsomed is a leading Swiss medical technology company specializing in the development, manufacture, and supply of innovative injection systems for self-medication. With our solutions, we enable people worldwide to administer their medication safely, conveniently, and independently.

records.description:
**About This Role**
The Head of Corporate Quality is responsible for creating and managing the Global Biogen Quality Management System (QMS). The main areas of focus include Quality Systems, internal and external audits for cGMP compliance (including external vendors and CMOs), IT Quality, Technical Product Complaints, and Central Knowledge Management (including documentation).
  
  
This role is central to Quality and PO&T, managing risk, compliance performance, staying compliant with regulatory changes, and seeking opportunities to gain efficiency and effectiveness in the administration of PO&T’s cGMP systems. Additionally, the role is accountable for preparing semi-annual executive-level updates on the state of Biogen’s QMS and informing Executive Management of potential business risks due to a changing regulatory environment or systemic issues within the company. This role also serves as the principal liaison with the R&D Clinical Compliance organization and provides guidance for ICH conformance. Oversight includes biologic products, ASOs, small molecule products, gene therapy, devices, digital, and combination products.
  
  
*This role is hybrid- RTP or hybrid- Cambridge based.*
**Travel requirements**
: 25% – 50% depending on location. More travel required if not located in RTP.
  
  
**What You’ll Do**

* Implement integrated quality systems, policies, and standards applicable to all Biogen U.S. and international manufacturing sites and PO&T locations, including Baar, Cambridge, Netherlands, Solothurn, and RTP.
* Develop and maintain a risk assessment process for evaluating and monitoring all cGXP systems.
* Ensure regulatory inspection responses are assessed holistically.
* Establish clear goals and effective metrics that provide insight into industry benchmarks and applicable trends regarding cGMP compliance.
* Oversee external monitoring of regulatory updates (domestic and international) and incorporate changes into Biogen’s QMS as needed.
* Internal and external GxP and ISO audit programs, including risk management and audit program oversight.
* Ensure Biogen’s internal manufacturing sites, Quality Systems, and vendors operate in a state of cGMP compliance, with any risks appropriately communicated and escalated.

**IT QA Department**

* Oversee GxP IT computerized systems across Biogen, including underlying infrastructure.
* Define appropriate standards and manage lifecycle documentation and supporting processes to ensure compliant implementation and management through retirement.

**Lifecycle Management**

* Oversee process and compliance-related content (specifically documentation, including governing policies, process documents, and other similar GxP documents) in the electronic document management system.
* Protect, index, classify, and archive GXP records, digitally preserve vital records, manage records lifecycle, and translate GMP content needed in multiple languages.
* Oversee the PO&T training program, providing global guidance and standards to ensure appropriate GxP training is conducted.

**Technical Product Complaint Department**

* Develop and maintain policies and procedures to manage complaints in line with industry and regulatory standards.
* Identify strategy and provide direction to team members regarding complaint investigation, root cause analysis, CAPAs, regulatory responses, and launch readiness for new products.
* Ensure trending and reporting of complaint cases and metrics, including appropriate escalation and response to significant events.

**Global Management Review (GMR)**

* Act as the chair for the GMR, ensuring ongoing management review and awareness of Biogen Quality and compliance performance (in accordance with cGMP and ICH expectations).
* Prepare semi-annual executive-level updates on the state of Biogen’s QMS based on GMR outcomes.
* Establish short and long-term goals, objectives, and strategies for the Global Corporate Quality organization.
* Ensure appropriate policies and procedures are in place to measure, monitor, and report "actual" versus "planned" results.
* Drive major projects and programs for the Organizational Unit or Function to completion within schedule and budget.
* Manage multiple cost centers and determine the development of overall objectives and long-range goals of the organization.
* Interact directly with senior representatives of regulatory agencies, including the FDA and EMEA.
* Manage direct reports and managers of managers to increase their performance and effectiveness.

**Who You Are**
You are a seasoned leader in the pharmaceutical industry with an expert understanding of both U.S. and international regulatory requirements. Your influence within an organization is felt through consistent execution and strong leadership competencies. With excellent communication and change management skills, you're adept at leading and implementing change. You thrive in a highly regulated environment and have comprehensive knowledge of the pharmaceutical product development process.
  
  
**Qualifications**
**Required Skills:**

* Bachelor’s degree in a related field with a minimum of 15 years of leadership experience in the pharmaceutical industry.
* Minimum of 10 years’ experience leading a Quality Assurance, Regulatory, or Corporate organization at the Director+ level in a highly regulated environment, preferably in biotech, pharmaceutical, or similar industry.
* Experience with the FDA, EMEA, and preferably multiple additional regulatory agencies in other foreign countries.
* Experience in clinical and commercial products as well as both large and small molecule programs, device, and combination products is strongly preferred. ASQ or other auditing certification is beneficial.
* Quality and Compliance experience consistent with worldwide regulatory requirements.
* Expert knowledge of US and International cGxPs, ISO, ICH, and Device regulations.
* Ability to hire and retain top talent with a track record of developing leaders.
* Excellent knowledge of the pharmaceutical product development process, ICH, and device regulations.
* Ability to influence the organization through consistent execution of Biogen leadership competencies.
* Strong leadership abilities required to effectively manage highly capable and high-performing teams.
* Demonstrated ability to lead and implement change, including excellent communication and change management skills.

**Preferred Skills**

* Advanced degree (PharmD, PhD)

Job Level: Management
  
  
**Additional Information**
The base compensation range for this role is: $281,000.00-$397,250.00
  
  
Base salary offered is determined through an analytical approach utilizing a combination of factors including, but not limited to, relevant skills & experience, job location, and internal equity.
  
  
Regular employees are eligible to receive both short term and long-term incentives, including cash bonus and equity incentive opportunities, designed to reward recent achievements and recognize your future potential based on individual, business unit and company performance.

and

**Vice President, Global Product Distribution Quality**

**The Opportunity**

Our client is a leading global medical technology company looking to appoint a hands-on VP Global Product Distribution Quality. Reporting directly to the SVP of Corporate Quality, you will be responsible for developing and implementing business strategies to effectively manage all global product distribution quality. The Global Head of Quality partners closely with executive leadership and cross-functional teams to drive continuous improvement, operational excellence, risk management, and organizational effectiveness while supporting ProSciento's strategic growth. Approximately 20% domestic and international travel is expected, with additional travel required based on business needs.

records.title: VP, Inventory Control & Quality Assurance
records.description:
Stord is The Consumer Experience Company, powering seamless checkout through delivery for today's leading brands. Stord is rapidly growing and is on track to double our revenue in the next 18 months. To meet and exceed this target, Stord is strategically scaling teams across the entire company, and seeking energetic experts to help us achieve our mission.
  
  
By combining comprehensive commerce-enablement technology with high-volume fulfillment services, Stord provides brands a platform to compete with retail giants. Stord manages over $10 billion of commerce annually through its fulfillment, warehousing, transportation, and operator-built software suite including OMS, Pre- and Post-Purchase, and WMS platforms. Stord is leveling the playing field for all brands to deliver the best consumer experience at scale.
  
  
With Stord, brands can increase cart conversion, improve unit economics, and drive sustained customer loyalty. Stord’s end-to-end commerce solutions combine best-in-class omnichannel fulfillment and shipping with leading technology to ensure fast shipping, reliable delivery promises, easy access to more channels, and improved margins on every order.
  
  
Hundreds of leading DTC and B2B companies like AG1, True Classic, Native, Seed Health, quip, goodr, Sundays for Dogs, and more trust Stord to deliver industry-leading consumer experiences on every order. Stord is headquartered in Atlanta with facilities across the United States, Canada, and Europe. Stord is backed by top-tier investors including Kleiner Perkins, Franklin Templeton, Founders Fund, Strike Capital, Baillie Gifford, and Salesforce Ventures.
  
  
**About The Role**
Stord is looking for a Vice President of Quality to build and lead the quality function across our fulfillment network.
  
  
This leader will own the systems, standards, and operating mechanisms that ensure inventory is accurate, processes are followed, and every order moves through our network the way it was designed to. The mandate spans the full lifecycle of inventory inside our buildings from inbound receipt and putaway through picking, packing, sorting, and outbound shipment.
  
  
This is an independent quality function. While our Operations teams are responsible for delivering volume efficiently, the VP of Quality is responsible for ensuring we never achieve speed, growth, or cost improvements by compromising inventory integrity or execution quality.
  
  
This leader should be an inventory and fulfillment quality expert at heart — someone who understands how inventory moves through a complex fulfillment operation, knows where process breakdowns create downstream failures, and is relentless about identifying and eliminating root causes.
  
  
**What You'll Own**
**Inventory Health & Accuracy**

* Own inventory health and accuracy across Stord's fulfillment network.
* Establish the standards, controls, and operating mechanisms required to maintain book-to-floor and floor-to-book inventory integrity.
* Own cycle counting, inventory reconciliation, adjustment governance, and inventory variance reduction.
* Build mechanisms to identify inventory defects early and systematically eliminate their root causes.
* Establish network-level metrics and reporting that make inventory health visible and actionable.

**Fulfillment Process Quality**

* Own process adherence across inbound, receiving, putaway, picking, packing, sorting, and outbound operations.
* Define the critical quality controls for each process path and ensure sites consistently execute against them.
* Build audit mechanisms that identify process drift before it becomes a customer or inventory issue.
* Partner with Operations, Product, Engineering, and Data to eliminate systemic sources of defects.
* Develop a clear view of transaction volume, exception rates, and defect rates by process path to identify where quality is breaking down.

**Lot Control & Regulatory Compliance**

* Own lot, expiration-date, and inventory-attribute accuracy across applicable customers and facilities.
* Establish controls for FIFO, FEFO, lot traceability, recalls, quarantine, and other regulated inventory requirements.
* Ensure Stord's operating processes meet applicable customer, regulatory, and contractual quality requirements.
* Build a quality organization capable of supporting increasingly complex and regulated categories as Stord grows.

**Continuous Improvement**

* Build a rigorous root-cause and corrective-action discipline across the fulfillment network.
* Turn recurring defects into permanent process, system, or training improvements rather than repeatedly solving individual incidents.
* Identify network-wide trends and deploy standardized improvements across sites.
* Partner with Product and Engineering to ensure recurring operational defects inform the technology roadmap.
* Create a culture where defects are surfaced quickly, investigated objectively, and permanently resolved.

**Quality Organization**

* Build and lead Stord's network Quality and Inventory Control organization.
* Establish clear ownership and accountability between Quality and Operations.
* Develop site and regional quality leaders capable of independently auditing operational performance.
* Serve as the executive escalation point when inventory integrity, regulatory compliance, or fulfillment quality is at risk.
* Maintain an independent point of view and be willing to stop, challenge, or redesign processes when quality standards are not being met.

**What We're Looking For**
We are looking for someone who has spent their career inside
**large, complex fulfillment or distribution operations**
and understands inventory at a level most operators do not.
  
  
**The Ideal Candidate**

* Has 12+ years of experience across fulfillment quality, inventory control, operational excellence, distribution, or supply chain operations, including significant leadership experience.
* Has led quality or inventory control across a multi-site fulfillment or distribution network.
* Comes from a scaled 3PL, retailer, e-commerce fulfillment network, food distribution company, or similarly complex physical operation.
* Is deeply fluent in inventory control, WMS-driven processes, cycle counting, reconciliation, lot control, and inventory accuracy.
* Understands the mechanics of inbound, putaway, pick, pack, sort, and outbound processes — and how defects in one process create downstream failures elsewhere.
* Has built quality systems based on data, audits, root-cause analysis, corrective actions, and measurable defect reduction.
* Is comfortable challenging Operations leadership when execution does not meet the required standard.
* Has operated in environments where quality and compliance cannot be traded for throughput or cost.
* Ideally brings experience from food, grocery, pharmaceutical, healthcare, or another environment with rigorous lot, expiration, traceability, or regulatory requirements.
* Can operate strategically at the executive level while still being willing to go onto the warehouse floor, trace an inventory discrepancy through a WMS, and understand exactly where a process failed.

**Company Description**
The Father’s Table is a privately owned national dessert manufacturer based in sunny Sanford, Florida, known for its innovation and extensive product lines. The company serves multiple channels, including national retail accounts, food service, wholesale clubs, convenience stores, and school lunch programs, reaching far beyond local bakeries. Its offerings range from grab-and-go convenience items to decadent, restaurant-quality desserts such as creamy cheesecakes and home-style cake rolls. A unique production process and strong company values have helped The Father’s Table become the #1 branded cheesecake in the retail in-store bakery segment. Applicants can learn more about the company by visiting www.thefatherstable.com.

**Director of Manufacturing**

Department: Operations Reports To: President ,Direct Reports: Plant Managers, Senior Manager of Cheesecake Production, Position Summary: The Director of Manufacturing provides strategic and operational leadership across two manufacturing facilities overseeing approximately 1,000 employees. This role serves as the primary architect of operational excellence moving the organization toward more data-driven decisions. The Director standardizes processes, drives toward modern manufacturing systems (KPIs, OEE, ERP), ensures food safety, and champions the successful implementation and optimization of our core cheesecake production lines.

---

**Primary Duties & Responsibilities**

**1. Change Management & Professionalization**

· Standardize Operations: Develop, implement, and enforce standard operating procedures (SOPs) across both plants to ensure consistency in quality, safety, and efficiency.

· Cultivate Leadership: Mentor, coach, and upskill plant managers and front-line supervisors, shifting the culture from firefighting to proactive, structured problem-solving.

· Data-Driven Culture: Introduce and track rigorous key performance indicators (KPIs) and Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE) metrics to guide daily, weekly, and monthly business reviews.

**2. Core Product Implementation & Optimization (Cheesecake Operations)**

· Product Optimization: Partner with the Senior Production Manager to evaluate all new cheesecake formulas, sizes, and configurations introduced into production.

· Constraint Assessment: Review new product introductions to assess potential issues or constraints affecting quality performance, labor efficiency, run rates, and operating costs.

· Executional Direction: Provide hands-on, "feet-on-the-floor" leadership to the operations team during major line optimizations, ERP system changes, and plant renovations.

**3. Food Safety, Quality & Compliance**

· Regulatory & Legality: Ensure both facilities strictly adhere to FDA, USDA, OSHA, and local regulations, taking ultimate responsibility for the safety and legality of all food products.

· Audit Readiness: Maintain "always audit-ready" standards for SQF, BRC, or other GFSI-benchmarked certifications and retail customer audits.

· Safety Culture: Champion a zero-injury safety culture through robust Hazard Identification, training, and behavioral safety programs.

4. Financial & Strategic Management

· P&L Responsibility: Manage the manufacturing budget, labor costs, variances, and operational expenses across both plants.

· CAPEX Planning: Identify, justify, and execute capital expenditure (CAPEX) projects aimed at automation, capacity expansion, and facility modernization.

---

**Required Qualifications**

· Experience: 10+ years of progressive food production operations management experience, with at least 5+ years in a multi-plant or regional leadership role.

· Scale & Product Expertise: Proven track record of managing a large workforce (500–1,000+ employees) in high-volume environments, with deep knowledge of automated bakery or cheesecake production processes.

· Transformation Experience: Demonstrated success leading an organization through a professionalization journey or significant operational scaling.

· Education: Bachelor’s degree in Food Science, Engineering, Business Administration, or a related technical field. An MBA or advanced degree is preferred.

· Certifications: Lean/Six Sigma Green or Black Belt highly desirable. Full understanding of SQF/BRC and HACCP systems.

---

**Physical Demands & Work Environment**

· Mobility: Must be able to travel between both manufacturing facilities on a daily/regular basis and spend significant time on the shop floor.

· Environment: Willingness to work in production environments with moderate-to-high noise levels (requiring hearing protection) and varying temperatures ranging from 45°F to 95°F.

* · Physical Capability: Ability to stand and walk for extended periods (up to 8–12 hours) during plant walkthroughs and occasionally lift or handle up to 35–50 lbs when assisting on the line

As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

We’re hiring a Director of Manufacturing Operations to oversee all production within our Air Dominance & Strike division, from rapidly maturing prototypes through full-rate production at scale.

As a Director in the Air Dominance & Strike Production organization, you must be a technical leader with the expertise to evaluate, qualify, manage, and advocate for an increasing number of sophisticated parallel pursuits. Success in this role demands consistent achievement across hardware production, team management, manufacturing operations, and financial goals. The ideal candidate combines technical acumen with effective communication, strong time-management skills, and a passion for leading transformative change. The ideal candidate should be energetic, highly organized, and deeply committed to scaling innovative products. While individual contributions are valued, teamwork is crucial for achieving the highest level of success while maintaining our Anduril culture above all.
  
  
*Please note: This role will be based at Arsenal-01 in Columbus, OH. A successful candidate will be expected to work out of Columbus, OH. Based on eligibility, relocation assistance may be available. There will likely be 25% - 50% travel required for the role.*

* Create a clear vision for Manufacturing Operations

+ Manage the portfolio of projects necessary to achieve your vision for Manufacturing Operations

* Collaborate successfully with leaders across our production organization

* Deliver quality products, on-time and at cost

+ Own attainment for both current and emerging programs

+ Maximize for what’s right both for Anduril’s future and maintaining a strong team culture
+ Coach, mentor and support Manufacturing Operations Managers and Production Supervisors
+ Create and maintain a high bar for excellence

* Clearly communicate up and out

+ Provide consistent and high-quality briefs both up, to Anduril Senior Leadership, and out, to AD&S Customers

* In summary, show up every day with a high level of urgency, ownership, and enthusiasm to get the job done

* 3+ years in a supervisor or production operations management role at the Director level or above
* 3+ years of experience as a manager of managers

* Experience working directly and communicating with designers and engineers
* A full understanding of the product life cycle (NPI to scaled production), LEAN manufacturing principles, and change management
* Extremely reliable, organized, and detail-oriented with excellent verbal & written communication skills
* You have a passion for employee development and enjoy the process of training and developing both new hires and veteran production staff

**Preferred Qualifications**

*New York, New York, United States (Hybrid – 3 days/week in office)*
Who We Are
  
  
At Pets + People, we make tails wag and customers smile with products brought to market through strategic licensing and innovation. Our brands make everyday life fresh, fun, and user-friendly for the whole family.
  
  
Our team of over 80 dedicated employees is headquartered in New York City with both national and global support. With our background, experience, and network, we are uniquely positioned to extend the reach of any brand to a new market.
  
  
“We’ve been a pioneer in licensing since 2008, translating favorite brands into practical ‘pet’ applications. In 2014, we expanded our vision into new markets within the ‘people’ sector. Now, we are leveraging our long track record of success and applying it both to pets + people.” – Steven Shweky, Top Dog
  
  
**About The Role**
Learn more about our capabilities at www.petspeople.com
  
  
We are seeking a dynamic and forward-thinking Director of Production to lead and evolve our global production organization within a fast-paced Consumer Packaged Goods (CPG) environment. This role is critical in driving operational excellence across both domestic and international production, while also reimagining how production can be more innovative, automated, and scalable as the business grows.
  
  
The ideal candidate is a hands-on leader who thrives in complexity, can manage a large SKU portfolio across multiple markets, builds strong global vendor partnerships, and inspires teams through coaching and mentorship. This person will lead on behalf of the department head when needed and serve as a strategic thought partner across the organization. We are open to candidates from a variety of industries, provided they bring transferable production leadership experience and a passion for continuous improvement.
  
  
What You'll Do
  
  
Global Production Leadership & Strategy
  
  

* Lead end-to-end domestic and international production operations, with ownership of the full purchase order (PO) lifecycle from placement through manufacturing, delivery, and payment.
* Develop and execute production strategies that support growth, scalability, and on-time delivery across multiple regions and manufacturing partners.
* Act as a senior leader within the organization, representing the production function and driving alignment across cross-functional teams.
* Proactively manage capacity, timing, and execution risk across a high-volume, high-SKU environment.

Innovation & Automation
  
  

* Identify and implement process improvements, automation, and system enhancements to improve speed, visibility, and decision-making.
* Reduce manual work and streamline production workflows across teams and departments.
* Champion data-driven production management through clear metrics, dashboards, and reporting.

Vendor & External Partner Management
  
  

* Build and maintain strong, collaborative relationships with domestic and international manufacturing partners.
* Establish and manage supplier performance metrics, including on-time delivery, lead time reliability, and execution accuracy.
* Drive continuous improvement and cost optimization across the production lifecycle.

* Act as the primary escalation point for vendor execution, capacity, and delivery risks.

People Leadership & Development
  
  

* Lead, coach, and develop a high-performing production team, fostering a culture of accountability, growth, and engagement.
* Build clear organizational structure, roles, and communication rhythms to support scale.
* Develop future leaders through coaching, feedback, and development planning.

Operational Excellence & Scale
  
  

* Strengthen operational rigor through standardized workflows and clear cross-functional handoffs.
* Identify and proactively address risks related to capacity, cost, supply continuity, and execution across domestic and international production.
* Ensure production operations are scalable to support rapid growth and evolving business needs.

What You'll Bring
  
  

* 10+ years of progressive experience in production, manufacturing, or operations leadership; CPG experience strongly preferred, but industry background is flexible.
* Proven success managing both domestic and international production operations.
* Experience managing and developing teams of 5–10; a hands-on people leader with a passion for coaching, mentoring, and team development within a lean, high-output team structure.
* Demonstrated experience leading complex production environments with large SKU counts.
* Track record of driving process improvement, innovation, and automation.
* Strong global vendor management and negotiation experience.
* Bilingual in Chinese and English preferred.
* Strategic thinker with the ability to execute at a detailed, operational level.
* Comfortable operating in an evolving environment.
* Strong proficiency in Excel; tech-savvy and resourceful, with a demonstrated ability to quickly adopt new systems, tools, and platforms as the business scales.

Hybrid Work
  
  
We're a hybrid office culture, in office 3 days per week with flexibility to work from home the rest. We value the connection and collaboration that in-person work brings, while giving our team room to work in the way that's most effective for them.
  
  
**Compensation**

The facility was honored with the 2014 Certificate of Recognition by the City of Wichita Falls, Texas, for its outstanding achievements in environmental excellence, including pollution prevention, waste minimization, and water conservation.
  
  
We are seeking an experienced and dedicated Plant Manager to oversee the operations of the Signal Hill power plant. * Comprehensive knowledge of ERCOT market operations and regulatory requirements.
* Demonstrated leadership skills with the ability to manage and motivate a diverse team.
* Excellent problem-solving and decision-making abilities.
* Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to build effective relationships with internal and external stakeholders.
* Commitment to safety, environmental stewardship, and operational excellence.

records.description:
Dart Container is seeking an experienced Plant Manager to lead our Conyers manufacturing operation and drive its next level of performance. This is an opportunity for a hands-on leader who wants to do more than maintain the status quo. You’ll step into an established operation with a strong foundation and a clear opportunity to shape what comes next.
  
  
We’re looking for a leader who can quickly assess the operation, identify opportunities, strengthen and develop the team, establish clear priorities, and move with urgency from strategy to execution. You’ll have the opportunity to tackle meaningful operational challenges, accelerate improvements, and see the results of your leadership firsthand.
  
  
If you’re a manufacturing leader who develops people, drives change, solves complex challenges, and turns plans into sustainable, measurable results, we’d like to hear from you!
  
  
**What You'll Do...**

* Lead the overall performance and direction of the manufacturing facility.
* Develop and execute a clear turnaround and continuous-improvement plan with measurable goals, owners, and timelines.
* ImproveOEE and operational performance, particularly within thermoforming.
* Strengthen predictive and preventive maintenance practices and ensure effective execution.
* Use strong business and financial acumen, including an understanding of P&L, to guide decisions and improve plant performance.
* Build, develop, and motivate a high-performing leadership team.
* Spend time on the manufacturing floor to understand challenges firsthand and build trust with employees.
* Identify operational gaps quickly, prioritize solutions, and drive change with urgency.
* Strengthen employee engagement while creating accountability throughout the organization.
* Lead change in a way that brings employees along and builds confidence in the direction of the plant.
* Establish clear KPIs and use them to measure progress and drive continuous improvement.
* Facilitate regular improvement planning sessions to identify key strategic opportunities to achieve manufacturing strategic goals and develop related action plans with measurable outcomes.
* Support and reinforce the effective application of the Daily Management System to validate that actions lead to desired performance improvements.
* Lead by example to promote and encourage employees to strongly commit to safety and GMP (Good Manufacturing Practices)
* Understand, support and follow management expectations in alignment with company values

**What We're Looking For...**
  
  

* Our ideal candidate brings:

+ Proven plant leadership experience in a manufacturing environment.
+ Demonstrated success improving or turning around manufacturing operations.
+ Strong knowledge of predictive and preventive maintenance and how to effectively implement maintenance programs.
+ Strong business acumen with an understanding of financial performance and P&L.
+ The ability to assess an operation quickly, identify gaps, and turn priorities into an actionable plan.
+ A track record of developing and leading high-performing teams.
+ Strong communication and motivational leadership skills.
+ The ability to build trust at all levels of an organization, especially with employees on the manufacturing floor.
+ A leadership style that combines urgency, accountability, integrity, and respect for people.
+ Thermoforming experience is a plus.

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering, Business or related field with seven (7) years of manufacturing operations management or leadership assignments demonstrating a progression of increased scope and responsibility

* Prior Plant Manager experience
* Experience managing multi-shift or continuous operations
* Thermoforming experience
* Knowledge of business and management principles involved in planning, resource allocation, cost analysis and budgeting, people management, and leadership guidance
* Displays strong interpersonal skills and is accessible and approachable
* Excellent verbal and written communication skills necessary in order to persuade and influence decision making of individuals, groups, or work teams
* Ability to utilize business sense and creativity to develop new ideas, approaches and solutions
* Ability to use logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions or approaches to problems

* Demonstrated project management experience
* Ability to be on-call 24/7
* Work is split between an office environment, production facility, and/or warehouse
* Exposure to extreme heat, loud noise, dirt, dust, odors, and fumes is probable
* Required to wear personal protective equipment (PPE) in required areas

**Preferred**

* Paper converting, chemical or plastics processing, or packaging industrial experience
* Lean manufacturing experience

Dart makes everyday products that give people the freedom to enjoy the food & drinks they love, wherever they are. This position is responsible for leading, planning, organizing, and managing the safe and efficient operation and maintenance of the Bison Generation Station (BGS) facility to economically produce electricity to satisfy member needs.

**ESSENTIAL DUTIES**

* Provide technical input for the decision-making process in power plant operation and maintenance. Keep plant staff informed of all aspects of the operation and maintenance of the facility and implement necessary corrective actions.
* Manage plant operational equipment; develop and maintain plant personnel and equipment safety standards; and develop preventative maintenance procedures and operational procedure manuals.
* Support the safety program by rigorously assuring standards are enforced and safety is at the forefront of all actions.
* Work in collaboration with other departments to build and adhere to all project budgets; responsible for developing and adhering to the BGS Long-Range Engineering Plan and the Capital Budget.
* Supervise the selection, training, development, and supervision of BGS employees.
* Evaluate the performance of plant section heads reporting to the position, review performance evaluations for all employees, and recommend salary adjustments for plant employees.
* Direct the development and submission of required reports to assure documentation and communication of plant operations, maintenance, and environmental activities.
* Authorize all plant purchase request orders and staff timesheets. In addition, review all proposed changes or modifications to plant systems or equipment and proposed tests or research programs.
* Responsible for staff development to ensure that each section functions safely and efficiently and that they all work together to meet the goals and objectives of Basin Electric, the plant operations division, and the station.
* Perform other duties as assigned.

**MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS**

* Bachelor’s degree in Energy Management, Business, or an Engineering Accreditation Commission/ Accreditation Board for Engineering and Technology (EAC/ABET) accredited engineering program; and 10 years of related power generation or petrochemical plant operations, maintenance, or engineering experience; or
* An associate’s degree in Power/Process Plan Technology or related field; and 12 years’ experience in power generation or petrochemical plant operations, maintenance or engineering; or
* A high school diploma or equivalent (GED or HSED); and 14 years’ in power generation or petrochemical plant operations, maintenance or engineering.
* Prior supervisory experience.
* A valid driver’s license.

**PHYSICAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL DEMANDS**

This position requires constant sitting; and occasional lifting/carrying up to 50 pounds, pushing/pulling up to 20 pounds, standing, walking, bending, crawling, reaching, and climbing. This position uses office equipment and field tools. This position also requires finger dexterity, good vision/hearing, hand coordination, and the ability to perform close work, analyze data/reports, conduct research, and implement recommendations. This position occasionally works in areas of dirt/dust, fumes, chemicals, extreme heat/cold, vibration, noise, and poor ventilation. This position must be respirator qualified.

**KEY SKILLS**

* Effective administrative and human relation skills.
* Excellent organizational, written and verbal communication skills.
* Proficient with personal computers and Microsoft Word, Excel, and Outlook.
* Able to provide work direction, develop plans/procedures/goals, and present information to others.

**A ROLE THAT SUPPORTS YOUR CAREER AND YOUR FUTURE**

* Competitive salary aligned with experience.
* Relocation package to support your transition.

* More benefits to support you.

**Duties And Responsibilities**

* Plant Operations: Review daily inventories and plan daily production. Conduct daily staff meetings to coordinate daily plant activities. Review daily load out schedule and coordinate with staff and milk movement personnel. Review daily production efficiencies and production reports. Review companies KPI’s, plant loss and assist in setting goals. Reports directly to the Director of Operations.
* Plant Quality: Review microbiology test results daily and direct further investigation of high counts. Review list of any out-of-spec. product with Food Safety Quality Assurance (FSQA) Manager. Review all product C of A's.

* Equipment: Verify that all plant equipment is in good working condition and all preventative maintenance is being performed on a scheduled basis. Review and approve all work orders. Review all daily maintenance activity reports. Develop capital justifications to update equipment as needed.

* Proficient in verbal and written communication skills. Must be able to communicate with upper management on a daily basis.
* Leadership, team development, coaching, and / or teaching experience.
* Good math and statistical skills.
* Excellent computer skills for data input, report writing, program tracking.
* Excellent organizational and follow through skills.
